# Getting Started

## Getting Started
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/start.html

New here? This section takes you from an empty chat to a published post: connect your channel, connect a sender bot, schedule the first message — then explore the tools that keep a channel running on autopilot. The three setup steps are short guides with pictures of what to tap. After that, the glossary explains any term you meet along the way, and the SetDate topic covers bulk-creating schedules from a file.

## Getting Started
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/getting_started.html

Three steps and your first post is scheduled. The whole setup usually takes five minutes. Step 1: Connect your channel Add @FastSchedulerBot as an administrator of your channel with at least the Post Messages permission. Then in the bot: Channels → Connect Channel , and send @yourchannel or simply forward any post from the channel. Step 2: Connect a sender bot — required Posts are delivered by your own bot; scheduling stays locked until every connected channel has one. Create a bot in @BotFather ( /newbot ), copy its token, and paste it in Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token . Then make your bot an administrator of the same channel, also with Post Messages. Step 3: Schedule your first message Tap 📅 Schedule a Message , enter the date and time ( 25.12.2025 10:00 ), type the post, preview, confirm. Done — it publishes itself. Each step has a detailed guide below, plus answers to the questions new users ask most.

Q: Do I need a sender bot to schedule messages?
A: Yes - every channel needs its own sender bot to post. After connecting a channel, create a bot with @BotFather (or use an existing one), make it an admin in your channel, and connect it in Fast Scheduler from Bots . Your own bot also gives a professional look, low sending delays, and detailed channel leaderboards.

Q: How long does it take to set up?
A: Most users are up and running in 5-10 minutes. Connecting a channel takes about 2 minutes, adding a sender bot takes 3-5 minutes, and scheduling your first message takes 1-2 minutes.

Q: What permissions does the bot need in my channel?
A: The bot needs at minimum the Post Messages permission. For full functionality (deleting/editing posts), grant Delete Messages and Edit Messages as well.

## Connecting a Channel
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/connect_channel.html

Before you can schedule messages, you need to connect a Telegram channel. Requirements • The main bot @FastSchedulerBot must be an Administrator in the channel • Give it at least Post Messages permission • For sender bots: the sender bot must also be an admin How to Connect 1. Add the bot to your channel as Administrator 2. In Fast Scheduler, go to Connected Channel 3. Click Connect Channel 4. Send the channel username: @yourchannel • Or forward any message from the channel • Or send an invite link • Or send the channel ID (e.g., -1001234567890 ) Multiple Channels • Free plan: 1 channel • Premium: up to 3 channels • Switch between channels at any time during scheduling • Set a Default Channel (Premium) to skip channel selection Removing a Channel • Go to Connected Channel → click on the channel • Scheduled messages for that channel will be paused Common Errors • "Bot is not an admin" — add the bot as admin in channel settings • "Channel not found" — check the username/link is correct • "Invalid format" — use @username or full invite link

Q: How do I connect my first channel?
A: Step by step: 1. Add the bot to your channel: Open your channel on Telegram → Channel Info → Administrators → Add Admin → search for @FastSchedulerBot → select it → grant at least Post Messages permission → confirm 2. Connect in the bot: Click Connected Channel on the main menu → click Connect Channel 3. Identify your channel: Send the channel username ( @yourchannel ) — OR forward a post from your channel — OR send an invite link — OR send the numeric channel ID ( -1001234567890 ) 4. Done! The channel appears in your list as connected. If you use a sender bot: also add your sender bot as admin in the same channel.

Q: Can I connect multiple channels?
A: Free plan: 1 channel. Premium: up to 3 channels. Each channel can have its own sender bot and schedule. To add another: click Connected Channel → Connect Channel → follow the same steps. You can switch between channels during scheduling by selecting the desired one.

Q: How do I set a default channel?
A: Premium feature. Step by step: 1. Click Connected Channel on the main menu (or use /channel ) 2. Select the channel you want as default 3. Click Set as Default 4. The default channel is now auto-selected during scheduling, saving you a step 5. To change it later: repeat the steps and choose a different channel 6. To remove default: go to the same channel settings → click Remove Default

Q: How do I remove a channel?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Connected Channel on the main menu 2. Find the channel you want to remove 3. Click the Remove button next to it 4. Confirm — the channel is disconnected Important: Scheduled messages for that channel are paused , not deleted. They remain in your account with all content and settings. If you reconnect the same channel later (using the same method as first connection), the messages resume automatically.

Q: How do I change a channel's timezone?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Connected Channel on the main menu (or use /channel / /timezone ) 2. Select the channel you want to configure 3. Click Timezone 4. Scroll through the list and select your timezone (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo) 5. The timezone is saved automatically All scheduled and recurring times for this channel will use the new timezone.

Q: How do I know which channel is connected to which bot?
A: Click Connected Channel on the main menu. Each channel in the list shows its assigned sender bot username below the channel name. To change the bot assignment: 1. Click Bots on the main menu 2. Select the bot you want to reassign 3. Click Change Channel and pick a different channel

Q: How do I set my channel's timezone?
A: Use the Timezone option when viewing your channel settings.

## Connecting a Bot
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/connect_bot.html

Every channel needs its own sender bot - a Telegram bot you own that posts messages to your channel under the bot's name. Why Connect Your Own Bot? • Messages are sent from YOUR bot, not the main bot • Your bot's name and photo appear as the author • Professional appearance for your channel • Low sending delays — your messages go out through your bot, not the shared main bot queue • Detailed channel leaderboards — see most viewed, most reacted, and most commented posts for each channel How to Get a Bot Token 1. Open @BotFather on Telegram 2. Send /newbot and follow the instructions 3. Choose a name and username for your bot 4. Copy the token (format: 1234567890:ABCdef..._XYZ ) 5. Never share your token with anyone you don't trust How to Connect 1. In Fast Scheduler, click Bots or use /bots 2. Click 🔑 I Have a Token 3. Send the bot token you copied from @BotFather 4. Select which channel this bot should send to 5. Make sure your bot is an Administrator in the target channel Limits • Free plan: 1 bot • Premium: up to 3 bots Managing Bots • Click Bots on the main menu to see all connected bots • You can replace a bot's token or disconnect it • Disconnecting a bot puts its channel back into "connect a sender bot" state — reconnect a bot to schedule again Inside Your Sender Bot • Management moves to the sender bot automatically when it is connected • Management → Hide Channel — strangers who start your bot won't see your channel name (Public Mode) • Management → Admins — give other people limited access to your channel • Statistics — open per-channel stats and leaderboards Troubleshooting • "Invalid token" — make sure you copied the FULL token from @BotFather • "Bot is not admin" — add your bot as an administrator in the channel • "Bot limit reached" — remove an existing bot or upgrade to Premium

Q: How do I replace a bot token?
A: If you reset the token in @BotFather (or it was compromised), replace it here: 1. Click Bots on the main menu (or use /bots ) 2. Tap 🔁 Replace Token under the bot 3. Paste the new token from @BotFather and send 4. The bot reconnects with the new token — scheduled messages resume automatically

Q: How do I disconnect a bot?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Bots on the main menu (or use /bots / /removebot ) 2. Find the bot in the list → tap 🗑 under it 3. Confirm Note: the channel is not deleted — it returns to the "connect a sender bot" state, and its scheduled messages wait. When you connect a new bot to the channel, everything works again.

Q: Can I use the same bot for multiple channels?
A: No, each sender bot can only be assigned to one channel. Each channel needs its own bot. This is a system limitation — if you have 3 channels, you need 3 sender bots (Premium). To see your bot-channel assignments: click Connected Channel on the main menu.

Q: Where do I manage my channel — main bot or sender bot?
A: In the sender bot . Management moves to your sender bot automatically when you connect it — no extra setup. Inside the sender bot you get the Management menu: Hide Channel (Public Mode) and Admins. The main bot stays as your hub for scheduling, settings, language, and Premium. If the sender bot's token ever breaks, Fast Scheduler falls back to the main bot so posts are not lost.

Q: What is Hide Channel and how do I use it?
A: Hide Channel is a privacy feature (Premium). When enabled, people who start your sender bot won't see your channel name. To toggle it: open the sender bot → Management → Hide Channel . Now when users start your bot, they see a generic welcome with an Open Main Bot button — not your channel name. Useful for keeping the channel private while the bot stays public.

Q: Why does it say my bot token is invalid?
A: The token format is: 1234567890:ABCdef...XYZ . Common issues: • Not the full token: Copy the ENTIRE token from @BotFather, including the colon and all characters after it — no extra spaces • Token was reset: If you used /revoke in @BotFather, you must use the new token, not the old one • Bot was deleted: If the bot was deleted in @BotFather, create a new one with /newbot To fix: click Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot → enter the correct token.

Q: How do I see statistics for my sender bot?
A: Per-channel stats and leaderboards are a Premium feature. Open Statistics in the main bot (or /stats) and pick the channel — the full view opens with average views, comments and reactions, plus leaderboards (views / comments / reactions) with period filters. Each channel row can also deep-link straight into the sender bot that posts there.

## Step 1: Link
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/onboarding_step1.html

Connect your Telegram channel to Fast Scheduler: 1. Add @FastSchedulerBot as an administrator to your channel. 2. Open the bot → Connected Channel → Connect Channel . 3. Send @yourchannel , forward a post, or send an invite link. The bot needs at least the Post Messages permission. Grant Delete Messages and Edit Messages too if you want the bot to manage posts.

Q: How do I start the onboarding?
A: Send /start to the bot. Onboarding walks you through connecting a channel and scheduling your first message in a few steps.

## Step 2: Schedule
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/onboarding_step2.html

Create your first scheduled message: 1. Tap Schedule Message in the main menu. 2. Pick the channel and enter the date and time (for example 25.12.2025 10:00 ). 3. Type your message — attach media if you like. 4. Review the preview and confirm. The message appears in the Calendar and the Message List immediately, and posts automatically at the chosen time. For regular content like daily digests or weekly roundups, set up a recurring message instead — it repeats on its own schedule until you pause or delete it.

Q: Which channel should I connect?
A: Every post is delivered by your channel's sender bot — the bot you paired with the channel in step 2. The main bot coordinates the schedule; your sender bot publishes under your brand.

## Your Account
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/start_account.html

Your account is created automatically the first time you open the bot - nothing to sign up for. • Your user ID is shown in /premium and is used by support to find your account. • Your language and time zone are stored in your settings. • Your plan (Free or Premium) controls your limits. To change language use /language ; to set your time zone use /timezone . To delete your data or account, contact @MaximalXP .

## Send Your First Post
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/start_schedule.html

1. Add @FastSchedulerBot to your channel as an Administrator (Post Messages permission is enough). 2. In the bot: Connected Channel → Connect Channel , then send @yourchannel or forward any post. 3. Connect a sender bot for the channel from Bots (create one via @BotFather or connect an existing bot) - required before you can schedule. 4. Tap Schedule Message , pick the channel, enter a date and time (e.g. 25.12.2025 10:00 ). 5. Type your message, attach media if you like, review the preview and confirm. That's it - your sender bot posts for you at the chosen time. See Getting Started for the detailed step-by-step guide.

Q: What is the fastest way to schedule a message?
A: Use /schedule , pick a channel, send the date/time and message, then confirm. For many posts at once, upload a .txt file in batch format.

## Quick Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/start_tips.html

• Use HH:MM alone to schedule for today at that time. • Upload a .txt file during scheduling to create many messages at once (blank line = new message). • Use Message List ( /list ) to edit or delete posts later. • Add a sender bot so posts appear from your own bot's name. • Set your time zone so times mean what you expect. • Anything you type in the bot works in both bots: @FastSchedulerBot and @SetDate_bot share your settings.

## Glossary
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary.html

Six terms cover most of the bot: • Channel — the Telegram channel your posts go to. The bot must be its admin. • Sender bot — your own bot that actually delivers the posts. Required for every channel; one bot per channel. • Scheduled message — a one-time post queued for a specific date and time. • Recurring message — a post that repeats (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly) until paused or deleted. • Signature — text appended to every post in a channel. • Premium — the paid plan: more channels and bots, unlimited sends, bigger media storage. Tap any term below for the full explanation.

## Channel
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_channel.html

A Telegram channel is where your audience sees your posts. Fast Scheduler connects to your channel, then posts your scheduled and recurring messages to it. You must be the owner or an admin, and the bot must be an administrator with at least Post Messages permission. Free plan: 1 channel. Premium: up to 3 channels, each with its own sender bot and time zone.

## Sender Bot
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_sender.html

A sender bot is a Telegram bot you create via @BotFather. Fast Scheduler uses it to post messages so they appear from your bot's name. Every channel needs one sender bot - connecting it is required after the channel is connected. Benefits: your brand on every post, lower sending delay, per-channel statistics and leaderboards. Each sender bot is assigned to one channel. Free plan: 1 bot. Premium: up to 3.

## Signature
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_signature.html

A signature is custom text that is automatically added to every message sent to your channel - for example "Posted by @yourbot" or your website link. It is a Premium feature. You can set the text, choose its position (start or end), and preview it before saving. When Premium expires, signatures are stripped from outgoing messages and removed at the final disconnect.

## Recurring
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_recurring.html

A recurring message repeats automatically on a schedule - every day, on specific weekdays, or on a monthly date. Use it for regular content: daily tips, weekly digests, monthly reports, birthday wishes, reminders. Free plan: 1 recurring message. Premium: unlimited. To stop a recurring message, delete it from Message List .

## Premium
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_premium.html

Premium is a paid subscription that raises or removes the free plan limits: • More channels and sender bots (3/3). • Unlimited scheduled, recurring, and sent messages (Free: 100 pending / 100 sends per month). • 20 media storage boxes, videos in storage, larger uploads. • Signatures, leaderboards, unlimited report schedules. Pay with Telegram Stars. See the Premium category for all details, including what happens when it expires.

## Import
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_import.html

Import brings data back into the bot from a file: a .fsback backup, a .txt list of messages, a .csv spreadsheet, or a schedule created in SetDate. Use Import from the main menu (or /import ) and send the file. Password-protected backups ask for the password you set when creating them.

## Export
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_export.html

Export saves your data to a file you can download and keep. You can export scheduled and recurring messages, or run a full backup (.fsback) that restores everything - channels, bots, settings, media. Use Export from the main menu (or /export ) for selective export, and /backup for a full backup.

## Media Storage
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_storage.html

Media storage lets you save photos, videos, and documents once, then reuse them in any scheduled message via From Storage . Items are kept until you delete them - they are never removed automatically while your Premium is active. Free plan: 1 box with up to 100 items. Premium: up to 20 boxes and unlimited items.

Q: What is media storage?
A: Media storage keeps your photos/videos in named boxes so you can reuse visuals across messages without re-uploading them.

## Feedback
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/glossary_feedback.html

Feedback is how you report issues, request features, or get in touch with support. Open Feedback (or /feedback ), choose a category, describe your issue, and submit. You can view replies to your reports under My Feedback .

## SetDate Integration
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/setdate.html

Need to schedule many posts at once? The SetDate Bot lets you bulk-create schedules in minutes. What is SetDate? SetDate is a companion bot that helps you create multiple scheduled messages quickly. Instead of entering each message one by one, you prepare all messages in SetDate and import them in one click. How It Works 1. Click Open SetDate during the scheduling flow 2. The SetDate bot opens with your context 3. Set a start date and how many posts per day 4. Define posting times (e.g., 09:00, 14:00, 18:00) 5. Send your messages — one message per block, separated by blank lines 6. Generate a schedule file 7. Click Import to Fast Scheduler 8. You return to Fast Scheduler with all messages pre-loaded 9. Choose media options and confirm Benefits • Schedule 10, 50, or 100+ posts in just a few minutes • Auto-assigns dates and times to each message • Supports European and American date formats • Supports inline buttons with custom layouts • Preserves all text formatting Features • Flexible time parsing: 08:00 , 2:00 PM , 12;00 • Upload .txt files with your posts • Download your schedule as .txt, .csv, or .json • Preview messages before importing • One-click import back to Fast Scheduler Language Sync Both bots share your language preference. When you change the language in one, the other bot sends you a message asking if you want to sync the change — tap Yes to apply it.

## Advertising & Promotion
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/advertising.html

To advertise to Fast Scheduler users, contact @MaximalXP to discuss placements and packages. For standard audience reach, Telegram's own Telegram Ads platform is also an option for public channels. Love the bot? Earn free Premium days by inviting friends - use /referral .

Q: How much does advertising cost?
A: Pricing varies depending on the placement type, duration, and reach. Contact @MaximalXP directly for a custom quote. Telegram Ads (native) have their own pricing at ads.telegram.org.

Q: Can I advertise my Telegram channel here?
A: Yes! Contact @MaximalXP to discuss promotional opportunities including sponsored placements, cross-promotion, and featured listings.

Q: Is there a self-service ad platform?
A: For Telegram's native advertising, use ads.telegram.org — it's a self-service platform. For custom placements within Fast Scheduler, contact @MaximalXP directly.

Q: Can I sponsor a specific broadcast message?
A: Yes, sponsored messages within bot broadcasts are available. Contact @MaximalXP to discuss your content, timing, and pricing.

# Scheduling Messages

## Scheduling Messages
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/scheduling.html

Everything about one-time scheduling: the basic flow, every content type the bot can post, and the tools to manage what you have queued. The basic flow 1. Tap Schedule Message (or send /schedule ). 2. Pick the channel — the bot you paired with it will do the posting. 3. Enter the date and time: use the format DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM (for example 25.12.2025 10:00 ) or send it in the same message as the text. 4. Send the message content — plain text or with photos, videos, documents, polls, stickers, voice, locations. 5. Review the preview and confirm. The post goes out automatically at the chosen time, in the channel's time zone. Before scheduling works at all, two things must be connected: the channel (bot as admin) and its sender bot — see Getting Started if you are not there yet. Managing the queue Everything you schedule lands in the Message List and Calendar : preview before it posts, edit any detail, or delete what changed. The topics below cover each content type and every management tool.

## Photo & Video Posts
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/schedule_media.html

Attach photos, videos, GIFs, or documents to any scheduled message. During scheduling, after sending the text, choose how to attach media: • Normal - one file attached to every message. • Random - each message gets a random file from the mix you sent (any types mixed). • Sequential - files are assigned in order, repeating as needed. • From Storage - reuse saved media. Free plan videos: up to 25MB. Premium: up to 50MB.

## Polls
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/schedule_poll.html

Schedule polls and quizzes for your channel. How to do it: 1. Create the poll/quiz in any Telegram chat first. 2. During scheduling, forward the poll/quiz to the bot. 3. Confirm - it is posted at the scheduled time. Note: only anonymous polls work in channels (Telegram rule). Regular polls with user names are not allowed in channels.

## Forwarding
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/schedule_forward.html

You can schedule a forward of an existing message instead of typing new content. During scheduling, forward the message from any chat. The bot copies its text and media into the scheduled post. You can then edit the caption before confirming. Forwarding is a fast way to re-post your best content at a later time.

## Formatting & Inline Buttons
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/formatting.html

You can use Telegram markdown-style formatting in your messages: **bold** — bold __italic__ — italic ___underline___ — underline ~~strikethrough~~ — strikethrough ||spoiler|| — spoiler `code` — inline code ```block``` — code block [text](url) — text link Note: URLs in text are not automatically clickable in sent messages. Use inline buttons for clickable links. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Inline Buttons — Full Guide ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Add clickable buttons at the end of any post. Basic Syntax &lt;inline&gt;Button Text&lt;link=&quot;https://url.com&quot;&gt; Multiple Buttons (Each on its own row) &lt;inline&gt;Buy Now&lt;link=&quot;https://shop.com&quot;&gt; &lt;inline&gt;Learn More&lt;link=&quot;https://info.com&quot;&gt; Side by Side with -- &lt;inline&gt;Buy&lt;link=&quot;shop.com&quot;&gt; -- &lt;inline&gt;Info&lt;link=&quot;info.com&quot;&gt; Result: [Buy] [Info] (same row) New Row with // &lt;inline&gt;Row1&lt;link=&quot;a.com&quot;&gt; // &lt;inline&gt;Row2&lt;link=&quot;b.com&quot;&gt; Result: [Row1] [Row2] Full Layout Example &lt;inline&gt;A&lt;link=&quot;a.com&quot;&gt; -- &lt;inline&gt;B&lt;link=&quot;b.com&quot;&gt; // &lt;inline&gt;C&lt;link=&quot;c.com&quot;&gt; -- &lt;inline&gt;D&lt;link=&quot;d.com&quot;&gt; Result: [A] [B] [C] [D] Important: • Use full URLs with https:// • Button text is limited to ~64 characters • Maximum of 8 buttons total (4 rows × 2 columns) • Buttons appear BELOW the message text Examples • Link button: &lt;inline&gt;Visit Site&lt;link=&quot;https://example.com&quot;&gt; • Side by side: &lt;inline&gt;Like&lt;link=&quot;t.me/yourbot?start=like&quot;&gt; -- &lt;inline&gt;Dislike&lt;link=&quot;t.me/yourbot?start=dislike&quot;&gt; Callback Buttons &lt;inline&gt;Action Name&lt;callback="action_data"&gt; Callback buttons send data back to the bot instead of opening a link — use them for actions, confirmations, and interactive posts. They follow the same layout rules ( -- for the same row, // for a new row) and can be mixed with link buttons. Important: • Button text is limited to ~64 characters • Callback data is limited to 64 bytes • Maximum of 8 buttons total (4 rows × 2 columns) • Malformed &lt;inline&gt; markup shows a warning — fix the syntax and resend • Callback buttons only work when the bot recognizes the data — you'll be warned before scheduling if a callback has no matching handler

Q: What formatting options are supported?
A: Supported: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, pre, spoiler (||text||), inline links, and inline buttons via [text=link="url"]. HTML tags also work if you prefer.

Q: Can I combine spoilers with other formatting?
A: Yes, spoilers work alongside bold, italic, and other formatting. Wrap the formatted text in || on both sides.

Q: Can I combine multiple formats?
A: Yes! You can combine formats. For example: *bold and _italic_* will show as bold and italic text.

## Supported Content Types (Free Plan)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/content_types.html

Here is everything you can send in your scheduled messages on the Free plan : ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Text ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Plain text or formatted text (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoiler, code, links) • Inline buttons with &lt;inline&gt; syntax — add clickable links • Polls and quizzes (send a poll from any chat and forward it during scheduling — only anonymous polls work in channels) • Text-only messages (no media attached) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Photos ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Single photos (JPEG, PNG) with optional caption • Photo albums (multiple photos grouped in one message — send them together during scheduling) • Random photo mode: send multiple photos, each message gets a random one • Sequential photo mode: photos assigned in order to your messages ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Videos ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Videos up to 25MB each • Supported formats: MP4, MOV, AVI • Can be sent with or without a text caption ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Documents & Files ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Any file type: PDF, DOC, XLS, ZIP, TXT, etc. • Animations (GIF) • Voice messages (OGG) • Audio files (MP3) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ What Requires Premium ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Videos larger than up to 25MB (up to 50MB on Premium) • Media Storage videos (not allowed on Free) • More than 1 Media Storage box (up to 20 on Premium) • More than 100 storage items (500 on Premium) • Everything else works on the Free plan! Tip: To see your current plan limits, use /stats or check the Plan Limits help topic. Need to send larger files? Upgrade to Premium with /premium to unlock up to 50MB video support and 500 storage.

## Media Selection Types
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/media_types.html

After sending your message text, you choose how media (photos, videos, etc.) is attached. 1. Random Mix Mode • Send multiple files during scheduling — photos, videos, documents, anything, even mixed together • Each scheduled message gets a random item from your collection, sent with the right method for its type • Different media each time — great for variety and engagement 2. Normal Photo Mode • Send one photo or video during scheduling • That single media is attached to every scheduled message • Simple and consistent — same image for all posts 3. Sequential Order • Send multiple media files in order • They are assigned in sequence to your messages • First media → first message, second → second, etc. • After the last media, repeats from the first • Choose order by date (upload time) or sent (input order) 4. From Storage • Use media you've saved in Media Storage • Pick from your saved collection • Saves time if you reuse media across multiple schedules 5. No Media • Text-only messages • No photos, videos, or files attached Tips: • For photo albums, send multiple photos in one batch using Normal mode • Videos must be under plan limits (Free: up to 25MB, Premium: up to 50MB) • You can mix text-only and media messages in the same batch

Q: Can I mix photos and videos in the same batch?
A: Yes! You can mix photos, videos, documents, animations, and voice messages in any mode (Random, Sequential, or Normal). Each message will get one item from your collection.

Q: What are the video size limits?
A: Free plan: videos up to 25MB each. Premium: videos up to 50MB when sent directly in messages, up to 50MB when saved in Media Storage.

Q: Does the bot support spoilers in media?
A: Yes. During scheduling, toggle spoiler on/off for photos and videos. You can also use ||text|| in messages for text spoilers.

Q: Can I schedule polls with multiple correct answers?
A: Yes. Quiz mode supports a single correct answer. Poll mode supports multiple correct answers. Choose the type when scheduling.

Q: What file types are supported?
A: Supported: photos (JPEG, PNG, GIF), videos (MP4, MOV, AVI), animations (GIF as animation), documents (PDF, DOC, XLS, ZIP, etc.), voice messages (OGG), audio files (MP3).

## Edit Messages
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/edit.html

Change the content, schedule, or settings of an existing message. How to Access: • From Message List : preview a message, then tap Edit • Use /edit followed by a job ID What You Can Edit: Text — change the message content Date/Time — reschedule for a different time Media — add, change, or remove attached media Channel — send to a different channel Recurring Schedule — change daily/weekly/monthly settings Editing a Recurring Message: • You can change the time, day, or interval • Changes take effect immediately for all future sends • Past sends are not affected Duplicate a Message (⧾ /dub): • Use /dub to create an exact copy of a scheduled message • Useful for creating variations of the same post • The copy starts in edit mode so you can change the date/time See also: Message List and Delete Messages .

Q: How do I find messages to edit?
A: Use Message List or Search to find the message, then preview and tap Edit.

Q: Can I duplicate a message?
A: Yes! Use /dub to duplicate a scheduled message into an editable copy with a new date/time.

Q: Can I change just the date/time without altering content?
A: Yes. Preview the message, tap Edit, then choose Date/Time. The text and media stay unchanged.

Q: Can I move a message to a different channel?
A: Yes. Preview the message, tap Edit, then choose Channel. Pick any of your connected channels.

## Delete Messages
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/delete.html

Remove scheduled or recurring messages you no longer need. How to delete: • From Message List : tap the 🗑 trash icon next to a message → confirm. • Use 🗑 Delete All at the bottom of the list — it removes all scheduled and recurring messages at once after a confirmation that shows exactly how many messages will go. • Use 🗑 Delete by ID and enter a job ID to remove one specific message (scheduled IDs look like s482913_7, recurring IDs like r482913_7 — you can copy them from the list). What happens after deletion: • Deleted scheduled messages are removed from the queue and will NOT be sent. • Deleted recurring messages are stopped and removed from the scheduler. • Deletion is permanent — it cannot be undone. Tip: to find a job ID first, use Message List or /search. Removing a channel is different — see Remove a Channel.

## Recurring Messages
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/recurring.html

Recurring messages repeat automatically - daily, on chosen weekdays, or monthly. How to create: 1. Tap Recurring Message . 2. Pick the channel and the interval (daily/weekly/monthly). 3. Set the send time. 4. Send the content and confirm. Free plan: 1 recurring message. Premium: unlimited. Manage them from Message List - edit time, pause, resume, or delete. Recurring messages expire after 365 days. See also: Pause & Resume for temporary stopping.

Q: Can I pause a recurring message without deleting it?
A: Yes. Step by step: 1. Click Message List on the main menu (or use /list ) 2. Find your recurring message (look for the icon) 3. Click on it → then click ⏸ Pause 4. The message will stop sending until you resume it 5. To resume later: click on the paused message → click Resume Unlike deletion, pausing preserves all settings so you can continue later.

Q: What happens to recurring messages when Premium expires?
A: If you have more than 1 recurring message, you'll see a Choose What to Keep menu on the first day after expiry. Select 1 recurring message to keep — the excess are paused (not deleted). If you reactivate Premium later ( /premium → choose a plan → pay), the paused messages resume. Free plan allows 1 recurring message which stays active.

Q: Can I edit the content of a recurring message?
A: Yes. Step by step: 1. Click Message List on the main menu (or use /list ) 2. Open the recurring list and tap the ✏️ button on your rule 3. Send the replacement (new text, new time, or both — media works too) 4. Confirm — the rule updates and all future sends use the new version The changes take effect immediately for all future sends.

Q: How do I change the time a recurring message sends?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Message List (or /list ) 2. Open the recurring list and tap the ✏️ button on your rule 3. Enter a new time (e.g., 14:30 for 2:30 PM) 4. For weekly: change the day as well. For monthly: change the day number 5. Confirm — the new time takes effect immediately The time is in your channel's timezone. To change the timezone: go to Channels → select the channel → Time Zone → pick your zone.

Q: Can I have multiple recurring messages?
A: Free plan: 1 recurring message only. Premium: unlimited. Each can have its own schedule, content, media, and target channel. To add more: click Recurring Messages on the main menu (or /recurring ) and follow the steps.

Q: How long does a free recurring message last?
A: Free plan recurring messages expire after 1 year from creation. Premium recurring messages never expire. You'll get a notification before a free recurring message expires with options to renew or upgrade. To check your status: use /premium or click Premium on the main menu.

## How You Can Use Recurring Messages
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/recurring_uses.html

Recurring messages handle most repeat-posting needs. A few common ways to use them: Daily Digest Send a daily roundup every morning: 1. Use Recurring Message , set it to repeat every day. 2. Enter the send time, e.g. 09:00 . 3. Write the digest content (or use the SetDate bot to prepare a full month). Event Reminder Remind your audience about an event: • Schedule an announcement at the event time. • Add reminder posts: -1 day , -3 hours , -10 minutes . • Use inline buttons for "Add to calendar" or "Buy ticket". News Roundup Post a daily or weekly news roundup: • Create a recurring message that runs on weekdays. • Use SetDate to preload a month of news scripts. • Attach a header image from your media storage. Promo Blast Schedule a promotion across channels: • Write the promo and add inline buttons ("Shop", "Learn more"). • Schedule it at your best posting time per channel. • Add follow-up reminders on days 2 and 5. Daily Quote Post a quote every morning: • Use a recurring daily message at 08:00 . • Prepare a month of quotes in SetDate and import them. • Optionally attach a matching image from storage.

Q: Can I schedule the same daily post for every day?
A: Yes — use a Recurring Message set to repeat every day with a fixed time. On Premium you can run unlimited recurring messages per channel.

Q: Can I schedule a one-time event post?
A: Yes — schedule a one-time message with the exact date and time. It sends once and stays in your Message List for review.

Q: Can news posts go out at the same time weekly?
A: Yes — use a recurring message repeating weekly on the day/time you want. Adjust the timezone first so the time matches your audience.

Q: How do I run a promo post series?
A: Schedule each promo as a one-time post (or a recurring series) with its own date and time, then preview before confirming. Batch scheduling via a .txt file makes large series fast.

Q: Can I schedule a daily quote?
A: Yes — a recurring message repeating every day at your chosen time is ideal for daily quotes. Change the quote by editing the recurring message.

## Pause & Resume
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/recurring_pause_resume.html

Pause and resume recurring messages without deleting them. How to Pause: 1. Open Message List (or use /list ) 2. Select Recurring Messages 3. Find the message you want to pause 4. Tap the ⏸ button next to it 5. Confirm the pause What Happens When Paused: • The message stops sending immediately • The message is NOT deleted — it stays in your list • The schedule is preserved • You can see it marked as 'Paused' in the list How to Resume: 1. Open Message List 2. Select Recurring Messages 3. Find the paused message (marked with ⏸ Paused) 4. Tap the ▶ button next to it 5. Confirm the resume What Happens When Resumed: • The message starts sending again on its schedule • No content or settings are lost • The next send happens at the next scheduled time Use Cases: • Seasonal content — pause holiday posts when out of season • Temporary breaks — pause during vacations or events • Testing — pause to review content before going live • Rotation — pause one message while another takes priority Tip: Pausing is better than deleting if you might want to use the message again later.

## Multi-Channel Scheduling
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/multichannel.html

Premium unlocks up to 3 channels, each with its own sender bot, schedule, and identity. How it works • Every channel pairs with its own sender bot — posts always appear from that bot's name. • When scheduling, you pick the target channel; a Default Channel skips the picker for your main one. • Each channel keeps its own time zone, signature, and settings. Everyday workflow • Switch the default channel when you focus on one project; switch back when done. • Use Message List with the channel filter to review one channel at a time. • Cross-posting the same message? Schedule it once per channel — a few taps with the Default Channel picker. Free plan covers 1 channel and 1 bot; Premium raises both to 3.

Q: Can I schedule the same message to all channels?
A: Not automatically. Schedule the message separately for each channel.

## Advanced Scheduling: Edit, Delete, Polls & More
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/schedule_advanced.html

Beyond the basic flow, the scheduler covers a set of practical extras. Here is the complete picture. Editing scheduled messages Everything about a pending message stays editable until the moment it is sent: open the Message List , tap the message, and choose 🔄 Replace (or use /edit with the job ID). You can change the text, the date and time, the attached media, and even the target channel. The bot shows a fresh preview before saving. Deleting messages Pending messages can be removed one by one from the Message List, via /delete , or by job ID. Delete All wipes every scheduled and recurring message for a channel at once — use it with care, the bot asks for confirmation first. Scheduling forwardable content Anything you can forward inside Telegram can be scheduled: forward a post from another channel while scheduling, and the bot copies its text and media into your own post. Polls and quizzes work the same way: create the poll in any chat and forward it to the bot during scheduling (or create it inline in the bot if your Telegram version supports poll sending), then pick a date. Only anonymous polls may post in channels — that is a Telegram rule for channels, not a bot limit. Special content types • Location and venues — send the location during scheduling. • Voice messages and video notes — recorded or forwarded as usual. • Animated GIFs and stickers — stickers can even carry a text caption, posted right after the sticker. Time zones Every date you enter is interpreted in the channel's time zone , so a channel with an international audience posts exactly when its readers are awake. Set or check it under Channels → the channel → Time Zone , or with /timezone .

## Can I Edit a Scheduled Post After Scheduling It?
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_edit_scheduled_post.html

Nothing about a scheduled post is carved in stone. Until the moment Telegram accepts the send, every part of it can change — that is the whole point of keeping a queue instead of posting immediately. What you can change Text and formatting — fix a typo, rewrite the hook, add links. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers and code all survive edits. Media — swap the image, replace the video, add or remove an album item. Send time — move the post earlier or later, or to another day entirely. Target channel — re-point a post to a different connected channel. Open the Message List (or /list ), tap the post, choose 🔄 Replace . The familiar schedule flow reopens with the post's current content pre-filled — change what you need and confirm. What editing cannot do Change a post that already published. Once the sender bot delivers the message to Telegram, it is a normal Telegram message — edit it with Telegram's own tools, not here. Edit recurring posts “in place”. A recurring rule is a single template that fires on its pattern — there are no separate per-day copies. Edit the rule so all future sends change. A workflow that actually works Channel operators who stay sane usually: schedule the week on Sunday, review the Calendar Monday, and treat edit as the normal verb — improving copy as the news moves. Edits are free, instant, and never notify subscribers. The only deadline is the send time itself.

Q: How late can I edit a post?
A: Any time before the send moment. If the bot is mid-delivery, the edit may not apply — that is the only race. For a post due within seconds, delete and reschedule instead.

Q: Can I edit a post that already went out?
A: Not from the bot — it is a regular Telegram message now. Telegram itself lets admins edit posted messages in channels; use Telegram for that.

Q: Does editing reset the monthly send counter?
A: No. The counter counts actual sends, not edits. Editing costs nothing.

## How to Schedule Many Telegram Posts at Once (Bulk Workflow)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_schedule_many_at_once.html

Scheduling one post at a time is fine for a meme; for a content calendar you want batch workflows. Fast Scheduler gives you three, and a full week can be set up in minutes. Way 1 — import a batch with SetDate The SetDate bot is the bulk tool: prepare messages as a set (text, times), then import them into Fast Scheduler in one click. It shines when you write copy in advance or migrate from another scheduler. Prepare → import → review in the Message List → done. Way 2 — let recurring rules do the repeating Anything that repeats should be a rule , not N one-off posts: “every day at 9:00”, “Mondays 18:30”, “every 6 hours”. Premium users get unlimited rules and no expiry; Free has one rule. Combined with a signature, a daily digest literally runs itself. Way 3 — stock the queue ahead The queue lets you stack up to 100 pending posts on Free (unlimited on Premium). The classic pattern: one writing session → schedule the whole week → check the Calendar view for holes and collisions → go live your life. Edits are free and instant, so the queue is your draft folder as much as your pipeline. Checking your work Three tools keep bulk work honest: Calendar — month at a glance; tap a day to see that day's posts. Message List — per-channel queue with previews; catch same-time twins here. Search — keyword search across everything scheduled, with per-result preview and edit for cleanup.

Q: Is there a true “upload a CSV of posts” feature?
A: Close: SetDate handles prepared batches, and /import accepts .json/.csv/.txt/.rtf/.odt files of messages. For calendar-scale bulk entry, SetDate is the intended tool.

Q: How far ahead can I schedule?
A: As far as your queue limit allows — up to 100 pending posts on Free, unlimited on Premium. Times years out are fine.

## How to Automate Recurring Posts in Telegram (Daily Digests, Weekly Roundups)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_recurring_guide.html

Anything your channel repeats should never be scheduled by hand twice. Recurring rules encode the pattern once — “daily at 9:00”, “every Monday 18:30”, “every 6 hours” — and the bot keeps generating posts on time, forever (or until the rule expires). Creating a rule 1. Tap 🔄 Recurring Messages in the bot (or send /recurring ) and follow the flow. 2. Compose the message — text, media, the works — exactly like a normal post. 3. Pick the pattern: daily, weekly (with weekday picker), or custom interval. 4. Set the time in the channel's time zone and confirm. The rule's future posts expand in the Calendar like any others, and the rule itself is listed with your recurring messages — so there is always a truthful picture of what will publish. Expiry — the part people forget On Free , the single recurring rule runs for 365 days , then expires with a notice — create a new rule to continue. It is the anti-zombie mechanism: dead rules can't silently post forever. Premium rules never expire, and you can run unlimited rules — one per content type is the usual pattern. Patterns that work in real channels Daily digest — a template message (“Top 3 of the day”) with the signature carrying credit; edit the rule weekly, not daily. Weekly roundup — Monday 9:00 rule; combine with the calendar to dodge holidays. Scheduled reminders — every-6-hours service posts for community managers; Premium's unlimited rules shine here. Editing and stopping Rules are editable — change text, time, or pattern, and future instances follow. Pause or delete when a campaign ends. Deleting a rule never deletes already-posted messages.

Q: Why did my recurring rule stop working?
A: On Free, rules expire after 365 days and you get an expiry notice — create a new rule to continue. Premium rules never expire. Also check the sender bot is still admin — a failed delivery stops the chain.

Q: Can two rules post at the same time?
A: Yes, and they will — in the order created. If they are too close together, Telegram may throttle the burst; space rules by a few minutes.

## What Types of Content Can You Schedule With Fast Scheduler?
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_media_types.html

A scheduling bot is only as good as the content it can carry. Fast Scheduler handles the full Telegram media palette, so your editorial plans never have to shrink to fit the tool. Everything you can attach to a scheduled post Photos — compressed automatically for fast delivery without visible quality loss. Videos — including size limits that scale with your plan (up to 25MB on Free, up to 50MB on Premium). Video notes (round videos) and voice messages . Audio files — full tracks with cover art preserved. Documents — PDFs, archives, anything Telegram accepts. Animations — GIFs and MP4 loops. Stickers — from any of your packs. Polls and quizzes — scheduled like any other post. Locations and venues — supported for per-post content. Albums and media groups Multiple photos or videos sent together are scheduled as one album and publish as a single media group — exactly how your followers expect it. You can also build a randomized pool : attach a mix of photos, videos, documents or any files and let the scheduler pick one per send, which is perfect for daily wallpaper or quote channels where variety matters. Text always travels with media Captions keep their formatting (bold, italic, links, spoilers) and your configured signature is appended to media posts as well. Inline URL buttons attach to media posts too, so a &ldquo;Read more&rdquo; button under a photo works out of the box. Limits that matter Uploads: up to 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium. Videos: up to 25MB on Free, up to 50MB on Premium. Media Storage boxes: 1 box with 100 items on Free — Premium multiplies both, so reusable assets live in the bot instead of your camera roll. Anything Telegram itself refuses (for example, a corrupted file) is rejected at scheduling time with a clear message — never discovered silently on the day of publishing.

Q: Can I schedule Telegram polls with Fast Scheduler?
A: Yes. Polls and quizzes are scheduled like any other message and publish through your sender bot at the set time.

Q: Can I schedule an album of photos?
A: Yes. Photos and videos sent together are scheduled as one media group. You can also attach a pool of mixed files and let the scheduler pick one randomly per send.

Q: What is the maximum video size for scheduled messages?
A: Videos up to 25MB on the Free plan and up to 50MB with Premium, in line with Telegram bots own upload limits.

## How Do I Format Telegram Posts? (Bold, Italic, Links, Spoilers and Buttons)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_formatting.html

Formatting is what separates a channel that looks professional from one that looks like a group chat. Fast Scheduler keeps every bit of it intact between scheduling and publishing. Rich text survives the whole pipeline Write a message anywhere — bold headlines, italic asides, underlined warnings, struck-through corrections, monospace code — and schedule it. Formatting is stored as Telegram entities , not flat text, so what publishes is pixel-identical to what you wrote: no mangled asterisks, no lost links, no broken emoji. Spoilers Wrap part of the text in spoiler markup and it publishes as a real Telegram spoiler — blurred until a reader taps it. Perfect for giveaways, answers, and sensitive details. The bot validates spoiler markup while you type, so unclosed pairs are caught at scheduling time, not in front of your audience. Inline URL buttons Add tappable buttons to any post with one syntax: [Button Text](https://example.com) . Use them for call-to-action links — &ldquo;Read the guide&rdquo;, &ldquo;Buy now&rdquo;, &ldquo;Join the chat&rdquo;. Buttons attach to text posts and to media posts alike. Keep button labels short (two or three words read best) and test one post before scheduling a whole campaign. Custom emoji Premium Telegram emoji in your drafts are preserved on publish, so your brand&rsquo;s custom smileys do not degrade into defaults. Signatures: formatting that stamps itself Configure a signature once — a footer with your links, hashtags or contact — and every scheduled post carries it automatically, on text and media alike. Signatures keep their own formatting, and you can override the signature per post when a particular message should go out clean. A checklist for polished posts One bold hook line first — most readers see only it in notifications. Links as buttons where possible; they out-click inline links. Spoilers for anything the reader should opt into. A signature so every post quietly advertises your next channel.

Q: Does Telegram formatting survive scheduling in Fast Scheduler?
A: Yes. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, links, spoilers and custom emoji are stored as Telegram entities and publish exactly as written.

Q: How do I add buttons to a scheduled Telegram post?
A: Use the syntax [Button Text](https://your-link.com) in the message. The bot converts it into a tappable inline URL button on the published post.

Q: Can every scheduled post have an automatic signature?
A: Yes. Create a signature once and it is appended to every scheduled and recurring post automatically, keeping its own formatting. Individual posts can override it.

# Channels

## Channels
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channels.html



Q: How many channels can I connect?
A: Free users can connect 1 channel. Premium users can connect multiple channels (up to the plan limit).

Q: Why can't I connect my channel?
A: Make sure @FastSchedulerBot is an admin in your channel with posting permissions. Also verify you're the channel owner or an admin.

## Add a Channel
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_add.html

To connect a channel: 1. Make @FastSchedulerBot an Administrator in the channel (Post Messages permission). 2. Open the bot → Channels → Connect Channel . 3. Send @yourchannel , forward a post, send an invite link, or send the channel ID (e.g. -1001234567890 ). Free plan: 1 channel. Premium: up to 3.

## Connect the Bot
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_connect.html

The bot must be an admin in your channel to post. Add it in channel settings: Administrators → Add Admin → search @FastSchedulerBot. Grant at least Post Messages . Grant Delete Messages and Edit Messages to allow full management. If you use a sender bot , it must also be an admin in the same channel.

## Manage Channels
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_manage.html

Everything about one channel lives in two places: the Channels list and the channel's own info screen . Channels (main menu) lists every channel you have connected. For each channel you get: • The channel name with a ⭐ marker on your default channel. • Time Zone — posts for this channel are sent in the channel's own time zone, so you never juggle UTC offsets yourself. • Change Channel — replace this channel with a different one; its scheduled messages move with you. • Disconnect Channel — unlink the channel (see Remove a Channel). • Set as Default / Clear Default — the default channel is pre-selected every time you schedule, so you skip the picker. Tap a channel's → button for the details screen: connection role, sender bot, time zone, and how many scheduled and recurring messages the channel holds. Each channel is configured independently — ideal for multi-channel setups.

## Default Channel
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_default.html

A default channel is pre-selected every time you start scheduling, so the channel picker is skipped and you go straight to your message. How: open Channels → find the channel → tap ⭐ Set as Default . The channel gets a ⭐ marker in the list; tap Clear Default on the default channel to remove the marker again. Setting a default channel is a Premium feature — free users see an upgrade prompt instead. You can still pick a different channel manually during scheduling at any time; the default only pre-selects, it never locks you in.

## Channel Permissions
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_permissions.html

For the bot to work, these admin permissions are needed: • Post Messages - required to send posts. • Edit Messages - recommended, for editing after posting. • Delete Messages - recommended, for cleanup. Add the bot as an administrator in channel settings and tick the permissions you want. Without Post Messages , scheduling will fail with a "bot is not admin" error.

## How Posting Works: Sender Bots
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_posting.html

Every post in your channel is delivered by a sender bot — that is what makes scheduling possible at all. This is not an optional nicety: the scheduler unlocks only after each connected channel has its own sender bot, because Telegram requires a bot to hold Post Messages rights in the channel it posts to. What this means in practice • Posts appear from your bot's name and avatar , not from @FastSchedulerBot — your brand stays in front of readers. • One bot per channel. A second channel needs a second bot (create as many as you like in @BotFather). • Free plan includes 1 sender bot; Premium raises this to 3. • If a send ever fails (say, the bot lost its admin rights), Fast Scheduler retries through the main bot so the post is not lost — and warns you to restore the bot's permissions. Connected a channel but not a bot yet? Open Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token and finish the pairing — scheduling, the calendar, and every other sending feature stay locked until then.

## Permanent Link
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_link.html

Your channel's permanent link is t.me/yourchannel (for public channels). You can send this link to the bot to connect the channel, or share it with your audience. Private channels don't have a public link - connect them by forwarding a post or sending the channel ID instead.

## Unlink vs Delete
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_unlink.html

• Unlink / Remove a channel - the bot stops posting to it; its messages are paused but preserved. • Delete a message - the scheduled/recurring message is removed permanently. Unlinking is reversible: re-connect the channel and everything resumes. Deleting is permanent - use it only when you're sure.

## Remove a Channel
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_remove.html

To unlink a channel: 1. Open Channels → find the channel. 2. Tap 🔗 Disconnect Channel → confirm. What happens to the channel's messages: • Scheduled messages on that channel are removed or reassigned to another connected channel — the bot tells you exactly how many. • Recurring messages are reassigned to another connected channel too; if none is connected, they stop. • If a sender bot was attached only to this channel, the bot notifies you that it no longer has a channel to post to. Re-connecting the channel later starts fresh — reconnect its sender bot before scheduling again. To delete individual messages, use Message List instead.

## Signature
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_signature.html

A signature is your custom footer (or header) — for example "Posted by @yourchannel" — added automatically when a post goes out. How: send /signature (or tap 📝 Signature on the review screen) → create a signature with ➕ Add Signature → choose its position ( start or end of the post) and how many blank lines separate it from the content. When saving you can enable auto-add and pick the channels it should attach to. • Saved signatures are reusable — edit, re-position, or delete them from Saved Signatures . • Signatures are attached at send time , so your stored messages stay clean. • Free users can try the feature once; after that it is Premium . See also: Signature Position.

## Channel Stats
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/channel_stats.html

Premium users can view per-channel statistics and paginated leaderboards: top posts by views, comments, or reactions (up to 50 per page), plus a top-commentators ranking of the people who comment most on your posts. Filtering: combine metric (views / comments / reactions / commentators), period (today / week / month / year / all), and page size (10 / 25 / 50) — then flip pages with the pager buttons. Comment authors: to see who actually comments, add the bot to your channel's discussion group. Until then, the leaderboard shows a tip reminding you — once the bot is in the group, comments are attributed automatically. These stats help you learn what content performs best so you can schedule more of what works. Channel stats are available for every connected channel — shown in the main bot, or inside its sender bot.

## How to Connect a Telegram Channel to Fast Scheduler (Full Walkthrough)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_add_channel_guide.html

Connecting a channel is a two-part handshake: the bot needs admin rights in the channel , and the channel needs to be registered in the bot . Here is the whole dance, including the steps people miss. Part 1 — make the bot an admin of your channel 1. Open your channel in Telegram → Manage Channel → Administrators → Add Admin . 2. Search for @FastSchedulerBot and add it. 3. Give it at least Post Messages . If you plan to schedule on behalf of other admins or use anonymous admin, keep the defaults sane. Part 2 — register the channel in the bot 1. In the bot, tap Connect Channel . 2. Give the bot what it asks for — any of these works: the channel's @username for public channels, a forwarded message from the channel, an invite link ( t.me/+… or t.me/joinchat/… ) for private channels. 3. Confirm. The bot verifies that it really is an admin there. Part 3 — pair the sender bot (mandatory) Every channel needs a sender bot — your own bot created via @BotFather — before anything can be scheduled. This is not optional: the sender bot is the account that actually publishes your posts, under its name. Fast Scheduler's main bot coordinates the schedule; the sender bot delivers. The in-bot wizard creates and pairs one in a minute; see the sender-bots guide for the detailed flow. The classic errors, decoded “Channel not found” — typo in the username, or the bot was not added as admin before you tried to connect. Add first, then connect. “Not an admin” — the admin rights were granted to a different bot than the one you connected. “Invalid token” — the sender-bot token got truncated on copy. Copy the whole thing: digits, colon, the rest.

Q: Can I connect a private channel?
A: Yes — via invite link or by forwarding any message from the channel during connection. Public username is not required.

Q: Why do I need my own bot just to post?
A: Telegram architecture: messages in a channel are sent by a bot account, not by your user account. Pairing your own sender bot also means posts appear under your brand, not a generic one.

Q: The channel connects but posts fail. First checks?
A: Sender bot still admin? Post Messages permission on? Bot not revoked in @BotFather? Those three cover nearly all post failures.

## How Do I Connect a Private Telegram Channel to Fast Scheduler?
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_private_channel_connect.html

Private channels are fully supported — the bot never needs to be able to search your channel, it only needs to be inside it as an admin. There are four accepted ways to point Fast Scheduler at a private channel, and at least one of them will take you under a minute. Before you start: give the bots admin rights Open your private channel → Administrators → Add Admin . Add @FastSchedulerBot with the Post Messages permission. That single permission is enough to schedule and publish. Then, inside Fast Scheduler, pair a sender bot and make it an admin of the same channel. This step is mandatory: every scheduled post is published through your sender bot , never through the main bot, so nothing in the scheduling flow unlocks until each connected channel has one. Four ways to connect the channel Open the bot → Channels → Connect Channel , then send whichever of these is easiest for you: @username — private channels have no @username, so this one is mostly for public channels. Forward any post from the channel to the bot. This is the fastest way for private channels: open the channel, long-press any message, Forward → Fast Scheduler Bot. The bot reads the source channel from the forward. An invite link — copy Invite Link from the channel menu and paste it into the chat. The channel ID — the numeric -100… identifier (e.g. -1001234567890 ) if you know it from another tool. Why the invite-link and forward methods are equivalent Both simply resolve your private channel to its internal ID. Fast Scheduler stores that ID plus your admin status; the channel&rsquo;s privacy settings never matter again after the connection is made. You can rename the channel, change its link, or toggle &ldquo;slow mode&rdquo; — the connection survives all of it. If connecting fails Bot is not an admin — re-check step one; the permission check runs live against Telegram. Invite link revoked or set to &ldquo;join request&rdquo; — regenerate the link, or forward a post instead. You are not the owner — the connector must hold admin rights in the channel under the account that talks to the bot. Free plan: 1 channel. Premium raises this to 3, each with its own sender bot, time zone and statistics.

Q: Can Fast Scheduler post to a private channel?
A: Yes. Private channels are connected by forwarding a post from the channel, pasting an invite link, or sending the -100 channel ID. The channel being private does not affect scheduling in any way.

Q: Does the sender bot also need admin rights in a private channel?
A: Yes. The main bot needs Post Messages to verify and manage, and your sender bot needs Post Messages because it is the account that actually publishes every scheduled post.

Q: How many channels can I connect on the Free plan?
A: Free includes 1 channel with 100 sent messages per month. Premium raises the limit to 3 channels with unlimited sends.

# Sender Bots

## Sender Bots
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bots.html



Q: Do I need a sender bot?
A: Yes - every channel needs its own sender bot to post. Connect one from Bots right after connecting a channel. Sender bots give you your brand name on posts, faster delivery, better security, and per-channel statistics.

Q: How do I create a sender bot?
A: 1. Open @BotFather in Telegram 2. Send /newbot 3. Choose a name and username 4. Copy the token 5. Add the bot as admin in your channel 6. Send the token to Fast Scheduler Bot

## Add a Sender Bot
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_add.html

1. Open @BotFather → /newbot → pick a name and username. 2. Copy the token (format 1234567890:ABCdef...XYZ ). 3. In the bot: Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token → paste and send. 4. Assign the bot to one channel. 5. Add the bot as an Administrator in that channel. Never share your token. Free plan: 1 bot; Premium: up to 3.

## Manage Sender Bots
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_manage.html

From Bots in the main menu you can see all connected bots and: • Open the bot in Telegram (tap its @username). • Replace Token after a reset in @BotFather. • Disconnect/Remove the bot. Disconnecting a bot hands the channel back to the "connect a sender bot" state — scheduling pauses until a bot is connected again. The messages themselves are kept.

## Sender Bot Management
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/sender_bot_management.html

A sender bot is more than a posting tool — it is also a full management interface for your channel. How it works When you connect a sender bot to a channel, management moves to it automatically — no extra setup. The main bot then shows a restricted menu (or a private "Public Mode" view if you hide the channel), while the full dashboard lives inside your bot. Inside the sender bot (Management menu) • Hide / Show Channel — in Public Mode your channel name is hidden from strangers who start the bot; they only see a generic welcome and an Open Main Bot button. • Admins — grant other Telegram accounts limited access to your channel: scheduling, viewing stats, or managing settings (RBAC). • Channel admins open the same bot and see exactly the tools their role allows — nothing more. Restore to the main bot? Not needed. Management stays with the sender bot; if the bot's token ever breaks, Fast Scheduler falls back to the main bot for delivery so posts are never lost.

## Bot Permissions
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_permissions.html

For a sender bot to post in your channel it must be an Administrator with at least Post Messages permission. Add it in channel settings: Administrators → Add Admin → search your bot's username → grant permissions. Optional: Edit Messages and Delete Messages for full management.

## Posting as Your Bot
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_sender.html

When a sender bot is assigned to a channel, all posts appear from your bot's name and profile photo instead of @FastSchedulerBot. This looks more professional and gives you per-channel statistics. Every connected channel must have a sender bot - connect one from Bots before you start scheduling.

## Bot Status
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_status.html

Check a bot's status under Bots - it shows whether the bot is connected and healthy. If a bot shows as disconnected, verify the token is valid (reset it in @BotFather if needed) and that the bot is still an admin in the channel. Messages queued while a bot is offline are sent as soon as it is back.

## Channel Stats & Leaderboards
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_stats.html

Per-channel statistics show how each channel's posts perform: totals, averages for views, comments and reactions, plus top reactions. How: open Statistics (main menu page 2 or /stats) → pick the channel under the overview. The full stats view is delivered via your main bot; each channel row can also deep-link straight into the sender bot that posts there. Leaderboards (Premium): inside a channel's stats, tap Leaderboard to browse top posts by 👁 views, 💬 comments, or ❤️ reactions — paginated, with period filters (today / week / month / year / all) and page sizes of 10 / 25 / 50 rows. Comment attribution (top commentators) works once the bot is in your channel's linked discussion group. These stats cover posts sent through Fast Scheduler only.

## Rotate Token
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_rotate.html

If your bot token was leaked, revoke it in @BotFather ( /revoke ) and update it here: Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot → paste the new token. Scheduled messages resume automatically once the new token is saved. Always rotate tokens immediately if you suspect a leak.

## Remove a Sender Bot
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_remove.html

To disconnect a bot: Bots → select the bot → Remove/Disconnect → confirm. The bot's token is removed from Fast Scheduler. Messages scheduled for its channel are paused , not deleted. If you later connect a new bot to the same channel, its messages resume automatically.

## Bot Fleet
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/bot_fleet.html

Premium users can run up to 3 sender bots, one per channel. Each bot has its own token, channel assignment, and optional management settings. Manage the whole fleet from the Bots menu. Keep tokens private - a leaked token lets anyone post as your bot.

## Do You Need a Sender Bot to Schedule Posts? (Yes — Here Is Why)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_sender_bot_required.html

Short answer: yes — a sender bot is required for scheduling and sending. The scheduling menu stays locked until every connected channel has one paired. Here is the why and the 60-second setup. Why the main bot cannot just post itself Two reasons, one technical and one yours: Architecture: channel posts are delivered by a bot account with admin rights. If @FastSchedulerBot delivered them, every message on every customer channel would carry the same name — and one bot hitting rate limits would slow thousands of channels. Your brand: with your own sender bot, posts appear from your bot's name and avatar. Subscribers see your brand, and your bot's admin rights are yours to revoke. Creating one in 60 seconds 1. Open @BotFather → /newbot → pick a name and username. 2. Copy the token (digits, colon, letters — the whole string). 3. In Fast Scheduler: Bots → ➕ Add Another Bot , pick the channel when asked, paste the token. Pairing is automatic. 4. Make the new bot an admin of the channel with Post Messages permission — or let Fast Scheduler promote it automatically when it can. Scheduling unlocks instantly. The in-bot wizard walks these exact steps and checks each one, so you cannot get the order wrong. Security, briefly Your token is stored encrypted and used only to deliver your posts. You can rotate it any time via @BotFather ( /revoke ) and update it in the bot — or remove the bot entirely, which deletes the token from Fast Scheduler's storage. If a token leaks, revoke it in BotFather first; a revoked token is dead everywhere. One bot per channel (Premium: 3×3) Free pairs 1 sender bot with 1 channel; Premium allows 3 bots across 3 channels. Multiple channels can share one sender bot, but the clean setup — one bot per channel — keeps branding separate and failures isolated.

Q: Can one sender bot serve two channels?
A: Yes, a sender bot can be paired with multiple channels you own. One bot per channel is still recommended for cleaner branding and simpler troubleshooting.

Q: What happens if I remove the sender bot from the channel?
A: Scheduling locks (no sender paired for that channel) and queued sends fail until you re-add the bot as admin. The schedules themselves stay saved.

Q: Is my bot token safe with Fast Scheduler?
A: Tokens are stored encrypted and never displayed in full after saving. Rotating the token in @BotFather instantly invalidates the old one everywhere.

## How to Manage Your Sender Bots: Rotate, Rename, and Keep Them Healthy
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_bot_management.html

Your sender bot is the public face of every post, so a little hygiene goes a long way. Everything below lives in Sender Bots (or /bots ) in Fast Scheduler. Check status before you check anything else The bots screen shows each bot's connection state and which channels it serves. If a send ever fails, this is the first screen: a bot showing disconnected means a revoked token or a BotFather change — fix it there, not in the schedule. Rotating a token (the right way) 1. @BotFather → /mybots → your bot → Revoke current token . 2. Copy the new token. 3. Fast Scheduler → Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot → paste. The swap is instant and schedules keep running. Do it the other way around (revoke and forget) and every send fails until you paste the new token. Rename = rebrand A bot's public name and avatar come from @BotFather ( /setname , /setuserpic ) — change them there and every future post instantly carries the new look. No re-pairing needed; Fast Scheduler stores the token, not the cosmetics. Fleet hygiene One bot per channel keeps branding separate and failures isolated (Premium: up to 3 bots). Remove bots you no longer use — removal deletes the token from storage; the bot account itself lives on in BotFather. After any BotFather change, glance at the status screen once — 10 seconds that prevent a silent failed-post day.

Q: Can I use the same bot for multiple channels?
A: Yes — a sender bot can serve several of your channels. Separate bots per channel remain the cleaner default for branding and debugging.

Q: I deleted a bot in BotFather. What happens in Fast Scheduler?
A: Its sends fail with an invalid-token error and the status screen shows it disconnected. Remove the bot from Sender Bots and pair a replacement.

# Admins

## Admins
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/admins.html

The Admins section manages who can use a connected channel and what they can do. It lives inside Sender Bots Management → Admins and is available to every channel that has at least one admin.

Q: How do I become an admin of a channel?
A: Anyone who is a real human administrator with the Post Messages permission in your channel can be listed as an admin. The list is synced live from Telegram — connect a channel and the bot discovers its admins automatically. Only the Main Owner (the channel creator) can manage the Admins section and change permissions. Other admins can use the features they've been granted.

Q: What happens if another admin of my channel activates Premium?
A: Premium is per channel : when any admin of a channel activates Premium, that channel's limits upgrade for everyone who uses it — other channels you have stay on their own limits. The upgrade is automatic and needs no action from the other admins.

Q: How do I request a permission I don't have?
A: If you tap a button you don't have access to, the bot shows "You do not have permission…" with a Request permission from the admin button underneath. Press it, optionally add a short message explaining why you need the permission, and the Main Owner gets a Yes/No request. One request per permission per week, so think about what you ask for!

Q: Do multiple admins get separate limits?
A: Yes — that's the whole point of the system. Every admin of the same channel shares the exact same quota: the monthly scheduled limit counts how many messages were scheduled this calendar month across all admins, and it never goes back down when messages are sent. Once the month's quota is spent, no admin can schedule more until next month (or until Premium is active for that channel).

## How Admins Share Limits
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/admins_limits.html

All message-related limits are counted per channel , never per user. Who counts: every admin of the channel — the Main Owner and everyone else — contributes to and shares one single quota. Two admins scheduling for the same channel consume the same budget. Monthly send limit (Free): counts messages actually sent to the channel during the current calendar month — up to 100. The counter never drops when messages are deleted; it resets on the 1st of the next month, or immediately when Premium becomes active for the channel. Pending queue cap: up to 100 scheduled messages can wait to be sent at once (per channel, shared). Pending scheduled cap: messages waiting to be sent for the channel, shared across all admins.
