URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/ms_box_manage.html

From inside a box you can: • Add, rename, move, copy, or delete items. • Search and preview media. • Replace a file. • Delete the box itself. Manage storage from Storage in the main menu.

## Save Media
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/ms_save.html

Save media to a storage box for reuse: 1. Open Storage → pick a box. 2. Send photos, videos, or documents to add them. Media is compressed on upload (see Media Compression). Documents and stickers are stored as-is.

## Manage Storage
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/ms_manage.html

All storage actions are available from Storage in the main menu: • Create/rename/delete boxes. • Upload, preview, copy, move, replace, and delete items. Items are kept until you delete them. If Premium lapses, the expiry cleanup may remove excess media.

## Storage Limits
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/ms_limits.html

Free: 1 box, up to 100 items total, no videos in storage. Premium: up to 20 boxes, unlimited items, videos allowed (up to 50MB). When you upgrade/downgrade, your saved media is kept; if your plan is reduced, storage beyond the free quota is handled during the expiry process.

## Storage on Premium
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/ms_premium.html

Premium storage benefits: • 20 boxes instead of 1. • Unlimited items instead of 100. • Videos allowed in storage (up to 50MB). • Larger uploads (100 MB). Upgrade via /premium to unlock them.

## Media Compression & Retention
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/media_retention.html

All media you send to the bot is automatically compressed &mdash; this shrinks the file Telegram stores and sends, and keeps it within your plan's size limits. Compression Comparison Feature │ Free │ Premium ───────────────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────── Photo max │ 1600px │ 2500px Photo quality │ Q65 │ Q90 Video max │ 620p │ 1080p Video CRF │ 28 │ 23 Video bitrate │ 1Mbps │ 2Mbps Audio bitrate │ 64k │ 128k Voice bitrate │ 48k │ 96k 4K media │ Blocked │ Allowed Compression is applied automatically when you upload media to: Media Storage, Scheduled / Recurring messages, Feedback attachments, Broadcasts, and anywhere else in the bot. Documents and stickers are stored as-is without compression. Media Retention & Cleanup The bot periodically removes old media references that are no longer needed: Ratings • Admin reply media in rating reviews: deleted after 30 days • The rating (stars, review text) stays forever Feedback / Support tickets • Attachments in closed / spam tickets: deleted after 30 days from closure • The conversation text stays forever Media Storage • Items are kept until you delete them manually • Never auto-deleted Scheduled Messages • Media reference is removed immediately after the message is sent • No data lingers Recurring Messages • Media stays until you delete the recurring message • Free accounts: recurring message expires after 1 year and is auto-removed

Q: Is my media quality reduced?
A: Yes. All photos, videos, audio files, and voice messages are compressed to save Telegram server storage. Free users get aggressive compression (photos 1600px/Q65, video 620p/CRF28, audio 64k). Premium users get gentler compression (photos 2500px/Q90, video 1080p/CRF23, audio 128k). On a phone screen the difference is barely noticeable. Free users are also blocked from uploading 4K media (photos ≥3840px or videos ≥2160p). Upgrade to Premium to send high-resolution content.

Q: How much smaller will my files get?
A: Typical savings depend on the original file: • Photos: free 60–85%, premium 30–50% • Videos: varies by source; a 50MB video at 1080p can drop to ~5–8MB for free users or ~15–25MB for premium users • Audio/Voice: re-encoded at the target bitrate, so a 320kbps file at 10MB would become ~2MB (free 64k) or ~4MB (premium 128k)

Q: Can I get my original uncompressed file back?
A: No. Once the bot compresses a file, only the compressed version is stored. Always keep your original files safe on your own device.

## Lifecycle
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/storage_lifecycle.html

Storage items persist until you delete them. When Premium expires, non-kept boxes are deleted on day 17 and the kept box is trimmed to 100 items (videos first). Renew Premium before day 17 to keep all media.

Q: What happens to storage boxes on expiry?
A: You keep one box you choose. Day 17: other boxes are deleted and your kept box is trimmed to 100 items. Renew before then to keep everything.

## What Is Media Storage and How Do You Use It Without Losing Your Mind?
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_media_storage_guide.html

Media Storage is your in-bot asset library: save a photo, video, or document once, then reuse it in any scheduled post without re-uploading. If you repost evergreen content or reuse brand imagery, this is the feature that saves the most time per week. Boxes: folders with a purpose Assets live in boxes — named containers like “Brand”, “Memes”, “Product shots”. Free gets 1 box with 100 items (no video in storage); Premium gets 20 boxes × 500 items with video support. Boxes keep the picker fast and your library mentally organized — one box per campaign is a good default. Saving and reusing Save: forward or upload media to the storage, or save straight from a scheduled message you are composing. Reuse: while scheduling, open the storage instead of attaching a file — pick the asset, done. Telegram file references are reused, so nothing is re-uploaded and quality is not recompressed per post. Organize: move items between boxes, rename, delete. The limits that actually matter Item count — the 100-item Free box fills fast with albums; delete stale assets or upgrade. Video on Free — storage refuses video on Free; schedule videos directly instead, or move to Premium for video-in-storage. Size — same upload caps as messages: 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium. A cleanup cadence that works Once a month: open each box, delete anything unused in 60 days, archive campaign boxes by renaming with a date prefix. Two minutes, and the picker stays a joy instead of an archaeology dig.

Q: Does deleting a media item break scheduled posts using it?
A: Posts keep working — a scheduled message holds its own reference to the media. Deleting from storage only removes it from the library for future posts.

Q: Can I share a box with another admin?
A: Storage is per account. To share assets, export them as part of a backup or send the files directly — the other account saves them into their own storage.

# Tools

## Tools
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tools.html

Four tools manage everything you schedule: • Message List — the workhorse. Browse messages per channel, preview, edit, delete. • Calendar — the month at a glance; tap a day to see its posts. • Search — keyword search across all scheduled and recurring messages. • Statistics — sends, limits, and per-channel counters. All four are one tap from the main menu (second page), and each has a matching command: /list , /calendar , /search , /stats .

## Message List
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/message_list.html

View, preview, edit, and delete all your scheduled and recurring messages. How to Access: • Click Message List on the main menu or use /list • Pick a channel (if you have multiple) What You See: • Scheduled messages — shown with date, time, and preview • Recurring messages — shown with schedule info (daily/weekly/monthly) • Media type — photo, video, document, or text-only What You Can Do: • Preview — see the full message content and settings • Edit — change text, media, date/time, or channel • Pause/Resume — temporarily stop a recurring message without deleting it • Delete — remove individual messages • Delete All — remove all messages at once • Delete by ID — remove a specific job ID Pagination: Messages are shown 10 per page. Use Previous / Next to browse. See also: Edit Messages , Delete Messages , and Pause & Resume .

## Searching Messages
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/search.html

The search tool finds any scheduled or recurring message by its text — no scrolling through the calendar needed. How to search 1. Tap Search on the main menu (second page) or send /search . 2. Type a keyword or phrase. 3. The bot lists every matching scheduled and recurring message with its job ID and send time. 4. Results show job ID and send time — open one and you get the same preview and edit/delete controls as the Message List. What is searched • The text content of all scheduled messages. • The text content of all recurring messages. • Job IDs such as s_123 or r_456 . Search is case-insensitive, matches partial words ("hel" finds "hello"), and covers all your messages across every channel at once. Narrowing results Use more specific words — the bot matches any of them. To browse by channel or date instead of keyword, the Message List and Calendar tools are the better fit.

Q: What if I want to browse all messages?
A: Use Message List to browse messages by channel instead of searching.

## Search
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/search_messages.html

Find any scheduled or recurring message by keyword. 1. Tap Search (or /search ). 2. Send a word or phrase. 3. Browse the matching messages; tap one to preview, edit, or delete. Search is case-insensitive and matches partial words.

## Search Scoping & Filters
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/search_filter.html

While the search box matches any word you type, you can focus results before searching: • Open Search from inside a channel's context (via Bots → a connected bot) to scope results to that channel only. • Combine keywords: the bot finds messages containing any of them, so adding words narrows the practical result set. • Job IDs give an exact match — ideal when you know the ID from a previous preview or notification. For everything else — channel-by-channel browsing, month view, per-channel cleanup — the Message List and Calendar remain the fastest tools.

## Deleting Found Messages
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/search_delete.html

Every search result opens the same controls as the Message List: preview, edit, and delete . To clean up a finished campaign: search for its keyword, walk the results, and delete each message you no longer need. Deletion is permanent — the bot asks for confirmation and shows the removed job ID afterwards. Need to wipe everything for one channel? Delete All in the Message List removes all scheduled and recurring messages for that channel in one confirmed step — faster than deleting search results one by one.

## Statistics Dashboard
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/statistics.html

See your scheduling activity and how your posts perform. How to open: tap Statistics on the main menu (page 2) or send /stats. The overview shows: • Scheduled and recurring message counts right now • Messages sent today and total sent • Messages created in total • Connected channels Per-channel stats: every channel row opens its own view — total messages, average views, comments and reactions, plus the top reactions on your posts. Leaderboards (Premium): from a channel's stats tap Leaderboard — top posts by views, comments or reactions, paginated up to 50 rows per page, filtered by period (today / week / month / year / all). Comment attribution needs the bot in your linked discussion group. Only posts sent through Fast Scheduler are counted — manually published posts don't appear.

## Calendar View
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/calendar.html

See all your scheduled messages on a monthly calendar. How to Access: 1. Click Calendar on the main menu (page 2) or use /calendar 2. Select a channel (if you have multiple) 3. Browse the month — each day shows scheduled send times Features: • Navigate between months with Previous / Next buttons • Both scheduled (one-time) and recurring messages appear • Recurring messages are expanded across the month based on their schedule • Times are shown in your channel’s timezone Tips: • Use the calendar to spot conflicts or gaps in your schedule • If you don’t see a message, check its timezone setting • For channel-specific views, pick a channel when prompted See also: Timezone Settings and Message List .

Q: How do I see all my messages in a list?
A: Use Message List for a full list view instead of the calendar.

## How Can I See Views, Reactions and Comments on My Telegram Channel Posts?
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_stats_views.html

Telegram shows view counts under every channel post, but it never shows you trends : which topics overperform, what time of day your audience actually reads, which posts collected the most reactions. Fast Scheduler records the metrics of every post it publishes and turns them into dashboards you can browse in seconds. Where the numbers live Open Statistics on the bot&rsquo;s main menu (page 2) or send /stats . You get: Usage totals — lifetime messages sent, messages sent today, and how many schedules and recurring messages are currently active. Per-channel dashboards — for every connected channel: average views, comments and reactions per post, plus the top reactions your audience uses. Leaderboards (Premium) — your top posts ranked by the metric you pick: Views, Comments, Reactions or Top Commenters. Each board shows 10 entries per page and can be filtered by period (day, week, month, year or all time). What is counted — and what is not Statistics are recorded when Fast Scheduler publishes a post and Telegram reports back the post&rsquo;s metrics. Manually posted content that never passed through the bot is deliberately excluded, so the numbers describe your scheduled content honestly. Comments made in the discussion group under a channel post are picked up too, which is what powers the Comments metric and the Top Commenters board. Three ways to actually use this Find your format. Sort by Views for a month: if the top five posts share a pattern (length, media type, topic), schedule more of it. Time your channel. Compare identical formats posted at different hours, then move recurring messages toward the winning window — the best posting times guide below has the general playbook. Watch reactions, not just views. Views measure reach; reactions and comments measure resonance. A post with half the views but double the reaction rate is usually the better template.

Q: Does Fast Scheduler track posts I publish manually?
A: No. Only posts published through Fast Scheduler are recorded, which keeps your dashboards focused on your scheduled content strategy.

Q: Are statistics leaderboards free?
A: Per-channel averages and usage totals are available to everyone. Leaderboards that rank your top posts by views, comments or reactions are part of Premium.

Q: What metrics can leaderboards rank by?
A: Views, comments, reactions and top commenters — each filterable by day, week, month, year or all time, with up to 50 posts per page.

# Pro Tips

## Pro Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips.html

A collection of tips to get the most out of Fast Scheduler Bot. Pick a topic below — each has practical advice plus a quick FAQ.

## Backup Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_backup.html

• Create a backup regularly — before big changes or when Premium expires (a .fsback file is sent automatically on day 3). • Backup files include your channels, settings, and configured messages. • Store backups somewhere safe — e.g. Saved Messages in Telegram. • Use /import to bring everything back on a new device or after reinstalling.

Q: How often should I make a backup?
A: Make a backup before big changes and keep the auto-backup you receive when Premium expires (day 3). A backup restores your channels and settings.

## Bulk Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_bulk.html

• Schedule dozens of posts at once by uploading a .txt file — one date+message per block. • Use the same format as the examples: each date line followed by the message keeps them together. • Attach different media to each block, or send texts first and let photos attach in order. • Preview before confirming to catch wrong dates early. See Batch Scheduling for the format details.

Q: How do I batch-schedule many messages?
A: Upload a .txt file with date+message blocks (see Batch Scheduling for the exact format). The bot creates one scheduled message per block.

## Channel Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_channels.html

• Make the bot a channel admin with Post Messages (and Delete Messages for media cleanup). • Use @usernames or invite links when connecting channels. • Set the channel time zone so schedule times match your audience. • One channel = one sender bot keeps delivery reliable. See Channels for connection and management details.

Q: Why is my channel not posting?
A: Check the bot is still a channel admin with Post Messages, the timezone is correct, and the sender bot is connected.

## Feedback Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_feedback.html

• Always include your user ID (from /premium ) when contacting support. • Add screenshots or exact error text — they speed up fixes. • Choose the right category (bug / feature / general) so reports route correctly. • Check your feedback status — the bot keeps you updated via the Feedback menu. See Feedback for how to submit.

Q: What should I include in a bug report?
A: Your user ID, the exact error or screenshot, the channel involved, and what you expected to happen. This helps us fix it faster.

## Language Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_language.html

• Change language with /language — it applies immediately. • Set your timezone in the same settings area so schedule times align. • If your language is missing, use Feedback to request it — new languages are added over time. See Language for the full list.

Q: How do I switch the bot language?
A: Send /language and pick your language. It applies immediately to all your channels.

## Migration Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_migration.html

• Moving to a new phone? Install the bot and connect the same channels as admin. • Use /import to restore settings and messages from a backup file. • Your Premium is tied to your Telegram account, so it follows you automatically.

## Payment Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_payment.html

• Telegram Stars monthly plans renew automatically; 3-month, 6-month, and yearly plans are one-time purchases. • Keep payment receipts — they help support verify issues quickly. • Redeem promo codes before they expire. • Yearly plans are the best value per day. See Payments for how each method works.

Q: Which payment method activates Premium fastest?
A: Telegram Stars activates instantly. See Payments for details.

## Premium Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_premium.html

• Review Premium periodically to know your limits and usage. • Recurring messages are unlimited on Premium — automate your digests. • On expiry, use the Choose What to Keep menu to pick the channel you keep. • Renew before day 35+12h to restore everything instantly. See Premium and Premium Expiry for details.

Q: What is the best Premium plan?
A: Yearly plans give the best daily price. Compare plans in /premium to pick what fits your volume.

## Preview Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_preview.html

• Always preview before confirming a scheduled message. • The preview shows text, media, time, channel, and options. • You can edit a preview — change time, channel, or content — before it's saved. • Use Message List to re-open any message for preview later.

Q: Can I edit a message after I preview it?
A: Yes — the preview lets you change time, channel, or content before confirming. After saving, edit it via Message List.

## Queue Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_queue.html

• Messages are processed in schedule order — earliest time first. • If many messages share the same time, they send in creation order. • Missed send windows are handled gracefully; check your sent reports. • Use reports for a send confirmation after each batch.

Q: What order are queued messages sent?
A: Earliest scheduled time first; equal times are sent in creation order. Check sent reports for confirmations.

## Recurring Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_recurring.html

• Use recurring messages for daily digests, weekly roundups, or monthly posts. • Premium unlocks unlimited recurring messages. • Recurring messages count separately from one-time scheduled messages. • On Premium expiry you keep up to 1 recurring message — choose which. See Recurring for setup.

Q: Can recurring messages be paused?
A: Yes — open the recurring message in Message List to pause, edit, or delete it. Paused messages stop sending until resumed.

## Referral Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_referral.html

• Share your invite link everywhere — groups, channels, your bio. • Friends must join and send enough messages for you to earn days. • Track your balance and referrals in /referral . • Watch for the minimum-message rule to avoid abuse. See Referral for rules and rewards.

Q: When do I get referral rewards?
A: After invited friends join and send at least 1 messages. Track your balance in /referral .

## Search Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_search.html

• Search matches keywords and partial words, case-insensitively. • You can search by job ID (e.g. s_123 ). • Search covers all your channels at once. • Found messages can be previewed, edited, or deleted right from results. See Search for usage.

Q: Does search work across all channels?
A: Yes — search covers all your scheduled and recurring messages across every channel at once.

## Security Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_security.html

• Enable Telegram two-step verification on your account. • Never share your bot token or payment details in chat. • Only grant channel admin (Post Messages) to the bot and your sender bots. • Revoke sender bot access from devices you no longer use.

## Signature Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_signature.html

• Signatures are appended after message content — great for branding. • You can set a different signature per channel. • Keep signatures short; they count toward the message length limit. • Signatures are stripped when Premium expires (after day 3). See Signatures for setup.

Q: Can I use one signature per channel?
A: Yes — each channel has its own signature setting. Signatures strip automatically when Premium expires after day 3.

## Storage Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_storage.html

• Organize media into named boxes so messages are easy to reuse. • On Premium expiry you can keep one storage box; keep the one you use most. • The kept box is trimmed to 100 items (videos first) on day 17. • Use storage to resend the same visuals repeatedly without re-uploading. See Media Storage for the full guide.

Q: What happens to my storage on Premium expiry?
A: On day 0 you pick one box to keep. Day 17: non-kept boxes are deleted and your kept box is trimmed to 100 items. Renew before then to keep everything.

Q: Can I store videos in Media Storage?
A: Yes. Videos are kept within the per-item size limits (up to 25MB for free / up to 50MB for Premium) and stored separately from photos, without quality loss.

## Time Zone Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_timezone.html

• Always set the time zone for each channel you use. • Times in the calendar are shown in the channel's timezone. • Use /timezone to check or change it quickly. • For audiences in a different region, schedule in their local time. See Time Zone for details.

Q: Why do my posts send at the wrong time?
A: Your channel timezone is used for scheduling. Change it with /timezone to match your audience.

## Troubleshoot Tips
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tips_troubleshoot.html

• Messages not sending? Check the bot is still a channel admin. • Media failing? Check size limits and bot permissions. • Late posts? Verify the channel's timezone and sender bot status. • When stuck, check the Troubleshooting category first. For step-by-step fixes, open the Troubleshooting category.

Q: Where do I start when something breaks?
A: Check the Troubleshooting category first. If it's still broken, use Feedback with your user ID, error text, and steps to reproduce.

## The Best Times to Post in Telegram (and How to Test Them Properly)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tg_best_posting_times.html

“Post at 9:00” advice is usually recycled guesswork. Here is what actually moves the needle on Telegram, plus a testing method you can run with a scheduler in one week. Windows that generally work Morning commute — 8:00–10:00 local time. News, digests, “start of day” content. Lunch dip — 12:30–14:00. Light, skimmable posts do well. Evening prime time — 19:00–22:00. The strongest window for most channels; long-form and media belong here. The key word is local . If your audience spans zones, anchor to your largest cluster's evening, and let the channel's time zone setting do the conversion for you. Consistency beats cleverness Subscribers learn your rhythm. A channel that posts daily at 9:00 trains its audience to show up at 9:00 — measurable in view-rate stability. This is the strongest argument for scheduling (and recurring rules) over manual posting: the schedule becomes a product feature. How to test slots properly 1. Pick two candidate slots (e.g. 9:00 vs 20:00) and alternate similar content between them for 7–10 days. 2. Compare views in the first hour , not totals — that is when your regulars arrive. Fast Scheduler's statistics screen shows view dynamics per post. 3. Keep the winner as a recurring rule, and re-test quarterly. Audiences drift with seasons and habits. Small things that quietly help Don't stack posts 5 minutes apart — spacing beats bursts for notification fatigue. Media posts slightly outperform text-only at equal times in most niches. Skip the “dump 6 posts at midnight” pattern; Telegram's own limits and your subscribers' patience both prefer a steady drip.

Q: Does Telegram show “time of post” that I can use for testing?
A: Views are timestamped; compare first-hour views across slots. The statistics screen gives you per-post numbers without extra tools.

Q: How many posts per day is healthy?
A: 2–4 for most content channels. Beyond that, watch unsubscribes — the metric that punishes oversharing fastest.

# Feedback & Support

## Feedback & Support
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/feedback.html

Every ticket goes to a human. Open Feedback in the bot (or /feedback ), pick a category, and describe the issue — attach a file or screenshot if it helps. What happens next • You get a ticket number immediately. • Replies arrive in the bot chat; you can continue the conversation in the same thread. • My requests shows the status of every ticket you filed. Bug reports with concrete details (job ID, time, what you expected vs. what happened) get fixed fastest. Keep it clean Feedback must not contain offensive language. One mild expression triggers a warning (the message is still sent); heavily offensive messages are blocked, and 3 warnings temporarily block new feedback. Mistaken flags can be reported from the warning itself.

## Send Feedback
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/feedback_new.html

1. Open Feedback (or /feedback ). 2. Choose a category: bug, feature request, payment, or other. 3. Describe the issue or idea clearly. 4. Optionally attach a screenshot. 5. Submit - support reviews and replies. Premium users get priority response time.

## Bug Reports
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/feedback_category_bug_detail.html

Report bugs under Feedback → Bug Report . Include: what you did, what you expected, and what actually happened. Screenshots and the affected feature help a lot. Bug reports with clear steps are fixed the fastest.

## Feature Requests

Request new features under Feedback → Suggestion . Describe what you'd like and why. Feature ideas that help many users are prioritized.

Report payment problems under Feedback → Payment . Include your user ID, payment method, and transaction ID so support can verify the payment quickly. See Premium Troubleshooting for common fixes first.

# Frequently Asked Questions

## Scheduling FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_schedule.html

Questions people most often ask about scheduling: formats, editing, limits, multiple channels, media, recurring messages, and more. Tap a question below to see the answer.

Q: Do I need a sender bot to schedule messages?
A: Yes. After connecting a channel, connect a sender bot for it from Bots - scheduling unlocks once every channel has its own bot. Posts then appear from your bot's name, and you also get lower delivery delays and per-channel statistics.

Q: Can I edit a message after I schedule it?
A: Yes. Open Message List (or use /list ), tap the message, then Edit — you can change the text, the date/time, the media, or even the target channel. Use /edit with the job ID for a direct shortcut.

Q: How many scheduled messages can I store?
A: Free plan: 100 pending messages stored at once. Premium: unlimited . If you go over the free limit you will receive a notice listing the excess; messages stay frozen but are not deleted.

Q: How many messages can I send per month?
A: Free plan: 100 sent messages per channel per calendar month . Premium: unlimited sends. There is no daily cap on either plan.

Q: Can I schedule the same message to multiple channels?
A: Each scheduled message targets one channel. Free plan: 1 channel . Premium: up to 3 channels , each with its own sender bot, time zone, and signature.

Q: Can I schedule a poll or quiz?
A: Yes. Create the poll/quiz in any chat and forward it to the bot during scheduling — or build it right in the scheduling flow, where supported. Note: Telegram only allows anonymous polls in channels.

Q: What media can I attach to a scheduled message?
A: Photos, videos, GIFs, documents, and albums. Free plan videos: up to 25MB (no 4K). Premium: up to 50MB with 4K support. Use Normal, Random, or Sequential media modes.

Q: Can I schedule a recurring message (daily / weekly / monthly)?
A: Yes. Free plan: 1 recurring message . Premium: unlimited . Set the interval and time, then manage it (edit, pause, delete) from Message List .

Q: Can I use HH:MM to schedule for today?
A: Yes. When entering the date, a time in HH:MM format schedules the message for today at that time. Full dates like 2026-08-20 14:30 also work.

Q: Can I upload a .txt file to schedule many messages at once?
A: Yes. Send a .txt file and the bot parses it into multiple scheduled posts. This is the fastest way to build a month of content — combine it with the SetDate companion bot.

Q: What time zone is used for my scheduled times?
A: Each channel has its own time zone (set in Channel Settings ), which defaults to your account time zone. Verify the listed time zone before confirming a schedule.

Q: What happens if my Premium expires during a schedule?
A: Nothing is deleted right away. Messages to non-kept channels stop sending after a grace period, and you get a prompt to download a full .fsback backup you can restore later with /import .

Q: How do I see everything I have scheduled?
A: Open Message List (or /list ). You can preview, edit, pause, or delete any scheduled or recurring message there.

Q: Can I schedule a forwarded message?
A: Yes. During scheduling, forward a message from any chat — the bot copies its text and media into the scheduled post. You can edit the caption before confirming.

Q: Can I schedule an album of photos?
A: Yes. Send several photos together during the media step and choose Normal mode — they post as a single grouped album.

## Sender Bot FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_bot.html

A sender bot is required for every channel: posts appear from your bot's name, with lower delay, better security, and per-channel stats. One bot per channel. Free: 1 bot; Premium: up to 3.

Q: Why should I add a sender bot?
A: A sender bot is required for every channel - posts are sent through it, so they appear from your own bot's name with lower delivery delay and per-channel statistics. Connect one from Bots before scheduling.

Q: How do I create and connect a sender bot?
A: Create the bot with @BotFather ( /newbot ), add it as an admin in your channel, then enter its token in Sender Bots Management . One bot per channel.

Q: Why is my bot not posting?
A: Make sure the bot is an admin in the channel, the token is correct, the channel is connected, and you have not hit the Free plan monthly send cap (100 per channel).

## Payment FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_payment.html

Everything about paying for Premium: methods, auto-renewal, cancellation, and refunds. Tap a question below for the answer.

Q: How do I pay for Premium?
A: Choose a plan in the Premium menu and pay with Telegram Stars . Premium activates immediately after payment is confirmed.

Q: Is the payment auto-renewing?
A: The monthly Stars plan auto-renews until cancelled. Prepaid 3-month, 6-month, and yearly plans are one-time — you buy a fixed period with no automatic charge.

Q: When does my Premium expire?
A: Your expiration date is shown in the Premium menu and in the status line under /premium . You will get reminders before it ends.

Q: Can I cancel Premium?
A: Yes, for the auto-renewing monthly plan: open the Premium menu and tap Cancel Premium . It stops future auto-renewal — you keep Premium until the end of the current paid period, then the standard expiry process begins. Prepaid 3/6-month and yearly plans never auto-renew, so there is nothing to cancel.

Q: Can I get a refund?
A: Refunds are handled case by case. Contact @MaximalXP with the payment details.

## Billing FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_billing.html

Billing details: methods, auto-renewal, renewed payments, and plan changes. Tap a question below.

Q: What payment methods are supported?
A: Telegram Stars . The monthly Stars plan auto-renews; 3-month and 6-month prepaid plans come with a 10% / 14% discount vs paying monthly and are one-time purchases; yearly Stars plans are also one-time purchases.

Q: Can I combine a promo code with a referral?
A: Promo codes and referral bonuses can both grant Premium time. For the exact stacking behavior and your current status check the Referral help section.

Q: What happens if my auto-renewal payment fails?
A: You get a bounded grace period with 'Automatic renewal failed' notices. If the charge never succeeds, the standard Premium expiry process begins.

Q: Can I switch plans later?
A: While Premium is active you can choose another plan when renewing. After expiry you re-subscribe from the Premium menu.

## Account FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_account.html

Your account, user ID, language, and data. Tap a question below.

Q: How is my account created?
A: Your account is created automatically the first time you use the bot — there is no sign-up form. Your Telegram identity is your account.

Q: Where do I find my user ID?
A: Open /premium — your user ID is shown in the status section.

Q: Can I change my account language or time zone?
A: Yes. Use the language menu to switch languages, and the time zone settings to choose how your scheduled times are interpreted.

Q: How do I delete my account and data?
A: Contact @MaximalXP to request deletion. If you want a copy first, download a full backup via /backup .

## Security FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_security.html

How your tokens and data are protected. Tap a question below.

Q: Where are my bot tokens stored?
A: Bot tokens are stored encrypted and used only to post on your behalf. Never paste a token into chats or send it to anyone.

Q: Is my data shared or sold?
A: No. Your data is not sold or shared with third parties except what is needed to process payments.

Q: Can someone log into my account?
A: No password-based login exists. Access is tied to your Telegram account — only you can control your channels and bots.

Q: How do I delete my data?
A: Contact @MaximalXP and request account deletion. You can also /export or download a full .fsback backup first if you want to keep a copy.

## Storage FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_storage.html

Media Storage saves photos, videos, GIFs, and documents for reuse. Tap a question below.

Q: What is Media Storage?
A: Media Storage saves photos, videos, GIFs, and documents so you can reuse them in scheduled posts via the From Storage mode — no need to re-upload every time.

Q: How much can I store?
A: Free plan: 1 box with 100 items . Premium: 20 boxes with unlimited items plus up to 50MB of videos per item.

Q: Are stored items ever deleted automatically?
A: No. Items stay in storage while you use the bot. On Premium expiry the non-kept storage boxes are cleaned up after the grace period — you choose which one (if any) to keep.

Q: How do I use a stored file in a scheduled message?
A: At the media step choose From Storage and pick the file you want, or use Random / Sequential to rotate through your saved media.

## Migration FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_migration.html

Moving your publishing setup between accounts, bots, or servers. Tap a question below.

Q: How do I move my messages to a new account?
A: Use /export from the old account to create a file, then /import in the new account. Either option. For everything at once use a full backup.

Q: What is the full backup format?
A: A .fsback file, created with /backup (Premium) or offered during Premium expiry. It contains your scheduled, recurring, channels, bots, media, and settings — restore with /import .

Q: Can I import data while keeping my new setup?
A: Yes. The import merges into your current account rather than replacing it wholesale.

Q: I got a .fsback file from the expiry download — how do I use it?
A: Send the file to the bot and use /import . It restores your data, so you can continue where you left off. No password is needed for the expiry backup.

## Tips FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_tips.html

Practical tricks to get more from the scheduler. Tap a question below.

Q: What's the fastest way to schedule for today?
A: Type a time like 14:30 when the bot asks for the date — it schedules for today at that time. No need to type a full date.

Q: How do I schedule a whole month quickly?
A: Upload a .txt file with one post per block; the bot parses them into scheduled messages. Or use the SetDate companion bot to generate a full month fast.

Q: Should I set a per-channel time zone?
A: Yes if your audience is global. Each channel can have its own time zone, so posts go out at the right local time per channel.

Q: How do I avoid gaps in my schedule?
A: Use the Calendar View to see which days are empty, and set recurring messages for the regular posts you never want to forget.

Q: What's the best way to run a big campaign?
A: Space it over several days instead of one burst to maximize reach, reuse on-brand media from storage, and take a backup before large changes.

## Troubleshooting FAQ
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_troubleshoot.html

Most common problems and their quick fixes. Tap a question below.

Q: My scheduled message did not send. Why?
A: Check, in order: the channel is connected, the sender bot (if used) is an admin with the token correct, the Free plan monthly send cap (100 per channel) is not reached, and the message is not paused or past its time.

Q: The message went out at the wrong time.
A: The channel's time zone (or your account time zone) decides local send time. Verify it in Channel Settings , then reschedule.

Q: I accidentally started a flow / nothing responds.
A: Type /cancel to abort the current flow and return to the menu.

Q: I paid for Premium but it is not active.
A: Payment confirmation can take a moment. Wait a few minutes and open /premium . If it still shows Free, contact @MaximalXP with the payment receipt.

Q: My media did not attach to the scheduled post.
A: Make sure you chose a media mode (Normal / Random / Sequential) during scheduling and that the file is within the size limit for your plan (10 MB free / 100 MB premium).

How Telegram platform rules interact with scheduled posts and payments. Tap a question below.

Q: What are Telegram Stars?
A: Stars are Telegram's in-app currency for digital purchases. You can use them to buy Premium from within the bot.

## Best Practices
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/faq_best_practices.html

Tips on when and how to post for the best results. Tap a question below.

Q: When is the best time to post?
A: Schedule at times your audience is active. Use your per-channel statistics to see which hours and days perform best.

Q: How should I structure a big campaign?
A: Space it over several days instead of one burst. Steady, consistent posting outperforms a random flood.

Q: Should I reuse media?
A: Yes — keep on-brand media in Media Storage and reuse it with Random or Sequential modes rather than re-uploading.

Q: Why back up before big changes?
A: A full .fsback backup lets you restore everything if something goes wrong during a rework, reconnection, or migration.

Q: What should I run as recurring?

## How to Move Fast Scheduler to a New Phone or Another Telegram Account
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_move_channel_account.html

Fast Scheduler stores your schedules in the cloud (on the bot's server), not on your phone. That makes moving house surprisingly painless — the only thing that really matters is which Telegram account owns the schedules . Same account, new phone Do nothing. Open Telegram on the new phone, log in, and chat with @FastSchedulerBot — your channels, bots, schedules and settings are exactly where you left them. There is no local app and nothing to sync. Different account (new number, team handover, second project) Schedules belong to the Telegram account that created them, so a new account starts empty. The clean path: 1. On the old account: /backup → include everything → save the .fsback / .fspback file. 2. On the new account: /start the bot, connect the channel , then pair its sender bot (this is mandatory — the sender bot is what actually posts). 3. Send /import with the backup file, choose Add or Overwrite . 4. Check the Message List and Calendar; confirm the time zone matches, then skim the first few upcoming posts. If you are on Free and your setup has more than one channel, temporarily move the extra channels out or upgrade — the restore brings everything over, but Free limits apply on the new account. Handing a channel to someone else permanently The same flow works for handovers: the new owner connects their own account to the same channel (they need admin rights in it), pairs a sender bot, and imports the backup you send them. After they confirm the Message List looks right, you can delete your own schedules to avoid double-posting — two accounts scheduling the same channel will post twice .

Q: Will my schedules keep firing while I migrate?
A: Yes — the old account keeps posting until you delete its schedules or the channel/bot setup changes. Pause or delete there before going live on the new account to avoid duplicates.

Q: Do I need Premium on the new account to restore?
A: No. Importing a backup is free. Premium is only needed for creating backups and for the extra channels/bots the backup may contain.

## Why Is My Telegram Channel Posting Twice? (Duplicate Posts, Explained)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_duplicate_posts.html

Double posts are annoying for subscribers and make a channel look automated in the worst way. The good news: the cause is nearly always one of four things. 1. Another account still schedules the channel The most common cause after a migration or team handover: the old account's schedules were never removed. Both accounts happily queue posts for the same time. Fix: in the other account, open Message List and delete its schedules (or disconnect the channel). If you cannot access the old account, remove the bot from the channel's admin list — that stops the posting immediately. 2. Two sender bots are admin in the channel Every channel must pair with exactly one sender bot, and that bot should be the only bot with posting rights. If you created a second bot and added it as admin, posts may arrive from both. Keep one sender bot per channel as admin; remove extra bots from the channel. 3. The message got scheduled twice Easy to do when re-sending the same text after an edit, or when importing while old schedules exist. Open the Message List for the day and scan for same-time twins before the posting window. The Calendar view makes clusters obvious. 4. The recurrence rule was duplicated, not edited Creating a new daily rule instead of editing the existing one produces two identical posts every day. Check the recurring list — if two rules share the same text and time, delete one. Still posting twice? Send /stats to see what is queued, then use /feedback with the channel name and two timestamps of a duplicate pair. Support can trace which connection produced each post.

Q: Does Fast Scheduler retry a post that failed, causing doubles?
A: A retry only happens when the send did not confirm. If Telegram accepted the post but the confirmation was lost (rare network hiccup), you can get one duplicate. It does not re-send confirmed posts.

Q: Can I merge two accounts scheduling the same channel?
A: Yes — export from the old account, import with Add on the new one, then clear the old account. Never leave both active.

## Telegram Channels vs Groups vs Bots: The Difference That Actually Matters
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tg_channels_explained.html

Telegram has three kinds of “places”, and content creators mix them up constantly. Here is the mental model that sticks. A channel is a megaphone One-way broadcasting: admins post, subscribers read. No reply threads by default (though a discussion group can be attached), unlimited subscribers, and posts carry the channel's name — or the name of the posting bot if “Sign messages with a bot” is on. Channels are where scheduled content lives. A group is a campfire Everyone talks. Groups are for community; up to 200k members in supergroups, full message history, topics if enabled. You do not “schedule to a group” the way you do to a channel — that is what channels are for. A bot is a worker Bots are accounts run by software. In your channel's context, a bot is the hands that type the message: a bot must be an admin with Post Messages for anything to be published. That is exactly why Fast Scheduler pairs a sender bot with your channel — your bot posts, under your brand. Why this matters for scheduling Want posts to appear at fixed times? Channel + scheduler + sender bot. Want subscribers to discuss the posts? Attach a linked discussion group to the channel — comments live there automatically. Want automation, menus, and commands? That is the bot layer — the part Fast Scheduler turns into a full publishing workflow. One nuance worth knowing: Telegram shows signed posts as “via bot” only when the admin chooses to sign with the bot; otherwise the post simply appears under the channel name. Either way, the sender bot did the typing.

Q: Can a scheduled post go to a group?
A: Fast Scheduler targets channels (including chat-announcement channels). Groups are conversational — schedule announcements to a channel instead.

Q: Do subscribers see which bot posted?
A: By default a channel post shows just the channel name. If the channel enables signing posts with the admin bot, the sender bot is credited.

## How Do I Schedule Many Telegram Posts at Once? (Bulk Scheduling with SetDate)
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_setdate_bulk.html

Scheduling one post is quick. Scheduling thirty — a week of content for a news channel, a course drip, a product launch sequence — needs a different tool: SetDate , the companion bot built for exactly this. The five-minute bulk workflow 1. Open SetDate. Open @SetDate_bot directly — or tap 📅 Use SetDate Bot whenever Fast Scheduler suggests it. 2. Feed it content. Send your messages one after another — text, photos, videos, anything you would schedule normally. 3. Choose a start date and how many posts should go out per day. 4. Define posting times — for example 09:00, 14:00 and 18:00 — and SetDate distributes your messages across that grid. 5. Send the batch back. One tap and every message appears in Fast Scheduler as a normal scheduled post, fully editable afterwards. Why this beats scheduling by hand One sitting instead of thirty. You write all content while you are in the writing mood, then let the grid place it. Perfect for recurring formats. A daily tip at 10:00 for the next two weeks is two fields in SetDate, not fourteen conversations. Everything stays editable. After import, each post is a regular scheduled message — search it, edit it, delete it, or move it in the calendar. Bulk for repeated content: recurring messages If the same message should repeat — a weekly digest, a daily reminder — you do not need bulk import at all: create a recurring message once and it reschedules itself. Free plans run 1 recurring message; Premium removes the cap (Unlimited) and its rules never expire. Tip: before importing a large batch, glance at your channel&rsquo;s time zone (see the time-zone guide) so the grid lands on the hours you actually meant.

Q: What is the SetDate bot?
A: SetDate is Fast Scheduler’s companion bot for bulk scheduling: you prepare many messages there, choose a start date and daily posting times, and import them all into Fast Scheduler in one click.

Q: Can I edit posts after bulk import?
A: Yes. Imported messages become ordinary scheduled messages — open the Message List or calendar and edit, move or delete any of them individually.

Q: How many posts can I import at once?
A: Imported messages count against your scheduled-message limit (100 pending on Free, unlimited on Premium), so a batch that fits your queue can be imported in one go.

## Telegram Channel vs Group: What Is the Difference and Which One Do You Need?
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/tg_channel_vs_group.html

New Telegram creators constantly mix these up, and picking wrong shapes everything after it — including how you schedule. Here is the short, practical version. The one-line difference A channel is a megaphone: only admins publish, everyone else reads. A group is a round table: every member can post and reply. A channel can have a linked discussion group , which adds a comment thread under every channel post — the best of both worlds. Choose a channel when… You publish content to an audience: news, deals, tutorials, drops. You want a clean feed readers can scroll without chatter. You care about per-post view counts — channels show them, groups do not. Choose a group when… Conversation is the product: support, community, coordination. You want members to see each other and reply freely. The classic combo Most serious projects end up with both : a channel for polished posts, plus a linked discussion group for the conversation under them. Telegram links them in the channel settings; from then on every channel post automatically gets a comment thread. Where Fast Scheduler fits Fast Scheduler publishes to channels — that is where scheduled broadcast content belongs. Because it also tracks the discussion-group comments under the posts it publishes, your statistics cover the conversational side too: average comments per post and Top Commenters leaderboards work with the combo setup out of the box. The practical recipe: plan and queue polished posts in the channel, and let the linked group absorb the discussion they spark.

Q: Can Fast Scheduler post to groups?
A: Fast Scheduler schedules to channels, which is the broadcast use case it is built for. For community discussion, create a channel with a linked discussion group — comments there are tracked in your statistics.

Q: What is a discussion group in Telegram?
A: A group linked to your channel in channel settings. Every channel post gets a comment thread in that group, giving readers a place to reply without polluting the channel feed.

## What Is Fast Scheduler? The Telegram Post Scheduling Bot Explained
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_what_is_fast_scheduler.html

Fast Scheduler (@FastSchedulerBot) is a Telegram bot that plans and publishes posts to your channels on a schedule — the missing native feature Telegram never shipped properly. You write content when inspiration strikes; the bot delivers it at the hour your audience actually reads. How it works in three roles The main bot (@FastSchedulerBot) is your control room: every conversation, every schedule, every statistic happens here. Your channel — connect it once by making the bots admins; the bot verifies rights and tracks it from then on. A sender bot — a small bot of your own (created in @BotFather in two minutes) that actually publishes the posts, so your channel&rsquo;s byline is your brand, not ours. Connecting one is required: scheduling unlocks only after each channel has a sender bot. What you can do with it Schedule anything — text, photos, videos, GIFs, voice, stickers, documents, polls, albums, with full formatting, spoilers and URL buttons. Recurring messages — a post that repeats daily, weekly or on custom patterns without re-scheduling. Bulk import — prepare a week of content in the SetDate companion bot and import it in one click. Statistics — views, comments and reactions per channel, with leaderboards of your top posts. Team features — admin permissions, shared channel limits, ownership transfer with confirmation phrases. Backups &amp; export — encrypted .fspback backups, JSON/CSV exports, migration between accounts. Free vs Premium, honestly Free : 1 channel and sender bot, 100 pending scheduled messages, 100 sends per channel per month, 1 recurring message — enough to run one channel seriously. Premium ($6.83/mo or $68.03/yr) : 3 channels and sender bots, unlimited scheduled queue, unlimited sends, unlimited recurring messages, bigger uploads (100 MB), leaderboards, backups, inline buttons and more. Who it is for News channels that publish on rhythm, creators who batch their week in one sitting, shops running drops at precise hours, and community managers who share channels with a team. If you have ever set a 3 a.m. alarm to post manually — this bot is the cure. Start here: open @FastSchedulerBot , press Start, connect your channel, pair a sender bot, and schedule your first post before your coffee cools.

Q: Is Fast Scheduler free?
A: Yes — the Free plan runs one channel with 100 pending scheduled messages and 100 sends per channel per month, forever. Premium at $6.83/mo lifts every cap and adds statistics leaderboards, backups and bigger uploads.

Q: Why does Fast Scheduler need a sender bot?
A: Your sender bot publishes the posts, so your channel’s byline is your own brand instead of a third-party bot. It is created by you in @BotFather and connected in two minutes.

Q: Can Fast Scheduler send messages to a Telegram channel automatically?
A: Yes. That is its core purpose: scheduled messages publish automatically at their set time through your sender bot, including media, formatting and buttons.

# Text Commands

## Text Commands
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands.html

Fast Scheduler Bot can be controlled with text commands — handy on desktop or when you open the bot from a search. Pick a command below for details, or use the main-menu buttons for the same features. Commands work with both the main bot and the @setdate companion.

Q: What other features are available?
A: Search finds messages by keyword. Statistics shows your usage. Calendar gives a monthly overview.

Q: How do I find my messages?
A: Use Search (/search) to find by keyword, or Message List (/list) to browse all.

Q: What is /cancel used for?
A: /cancel stops any active operation and returns you to the main menu. Useful if the bot is waiting for input and you want to start over.

Q: How do I use a promo code?
A: Go to Premium → Redeem Promo Code, or use /promocode. Enter the code exactly as provided.

## All Commands
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands_list.html

Here is the full command list: • /start — open the main menu • /help — help center • /channel — connect or manage a channel • /schedule — schedule a message • /recurring — create a recurring message • /list — see all scheduled messages • /search — search your messages • /calendar — monthly calendar view • /delete — delete messages or media • /bots — manage sender bots • /storage — manage media storage • /premium — view or buy Premium • /referral — invite friends and earn days • /language — change language • /timezone — manage timezones • /stats — usage statistics • /data — import/export hub • /export — export messages as a file • /import — import messages from a file • /backup — create/restore a backup • /feedback — feedback & support • /cancel — cancel any active operation • /dub — duplicate a scheduled message • /edit — edit a scheduled message • /signature — signature menu • /promocode — apply a promo code • /addbot — connect a sender bot • /listbots — list your sender bots • /removebot — remove a sender bot • /skip — skip the current step • /newchannel — connect a new channel Most features are also reachable from the main menu buttons.

## /schedule
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands_schedule.html

Starts the message scheduling flow. 1. Send /schedule (or press Schedule ) 2. Choose a channel 3. Enter the date/time (e.g. 25.12.2024 10:00 ) 4. Send the message text and/or media 5. Preview and confirm You can also schedule many messages at once by sending a .txt file — see Batch Scheduling in the Scheduling category.

## /search
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands_search.html

Searches all your scheduled and recurring messages by keyword or job ID. 1. Send /search 2. Type a keyword or part of the text 3. The bot lists matching messages across all channels 4. Tap a result to preview, edit, or delete it Search is case-insensitive and matches partial words. For browsing by channel use Message List ( /list ).

## /premium
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands_premium.html

Opens the Premium panel: your plan, limits, payment, and expiry info. From here you can: • See your current plan and usage vs limits • Buy or upgrade to Premium (monthly, 3-month, 6-month, or yearly) • Choose a payment method: Telegram Stars (in-app purchase) • Redeem a promo code • Cancel or re-enable auto-renewal • Check the expiry timeline if Premium ended See the Premium category for a full feature list and FAQ.

## /referral
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands_referral.html

Opens the referral program: invite friends and earn free Premium days. How it works: • You get a unique invite link • Friends who join and send enough messages earn you reward days • Your balance and history are shown here See the Referral category for rules and reward details.

## Settings
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands_settings.html

There is no single Settings screen. Each setting lives in its own menu or command: • /language — interface language • /timezone — timezones • /signature — default signature for new messages • /channel — connected channels and default channel Settings are stored per-user and apply across all your channels.

## /language
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/commands_language.html

Changes the bot's interface language. 1. Send /language 2. Pick your language from the list 3. The bot language switches immediately Your choice is saved per-user, not per-channel, and applies to all your channels in this bot. See also: Language category for FAQ about adding new languages.

# Troubleshooting

## Troubleshooting
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/errors.html

Something went wrong? Every error has a cause and a fix. Tap a question below — the most common cases (messages not posting, late posts, media failures, permission problems) each have a dedicated answer.

Q: How do I exit a stuck flow?
A: Use the /cancel command at any time to exit the current operation and return to the main menu.

Q: Payment went through but Premium didn't activate
A: Wait 2-3 minutes — there can be a small delay with some payment providers. If still not active after 5 minutes, check with /premium . If Premium still shows as inactive, contact @MaximalXP with your user ID, payment method, and transaction details.

Q: I used a referral link but didn't get Premium days
A: Referral Premium days are only credited when the referred person 1) is a NEW user (never used the bot before), and 2) connects a channel. Just starting the bot with the link is not enough. Check /referral to see your status. Contact @MaximalXP if requirements were met.

Q: My scheduled messages stopped sending
A: Check: 1) Your sender bot is still connected and is admin in the channel. 2) You haven't hit the Free plan monthly send cap (100 per channel). 3) The channel hasn't been removed. 4) Your Premium hasn't expired (if you had channels above the free limit). Use /stats to check your status.

Q: I accidentally deleted something — can I recover it?
A: If you have a backup (.fsback or .fspback file), you can restore it with /import . Without a backup, deleted data cannot be recovered. We recommend regular exports to avoid data loss.

Q: How do I delete my account or all my data?
A: Contact @MaximalXP directly to request account deletion. You can also manually delete your data using the export/backup feature first to keep a copy. Your scheduled messages, media, and settings will be permanently removed.

Q: Can I get a refund for Premium?
A: Refunds are handled on a case-by-case basis. Contact @MaximalXP directly with your payment details and reason for the refund request. Refunds are not guaranteed but are reviewed individually.

Q: My bot token was revoked by @BotFather
A: If you reset your bot token in @BotFather, the old token stops working immediately. Go to Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot and enter the new token from @BotFather. Your scheduled messages will resume once the new token is saved.

## Common Errors
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_common.html

• "Bot is not an admin" - add the bot as an administrator in the channel with Post Messages permission. • "Invalid token" - copy the FULL token from @BotFather, no extra spaces. • "Channel not found" - check the username/link; use @username or an invite link. • "Limit reached" - check /stats ; delete old messages or upgrade. Most errors are fixed by one of these. See Troubleshooting for the full guide.

## Network Errors
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_network.html

• Messages queue while the bot or Telegram is offline and send when it's back - nothing is lost. • If a sender bot shows disconnected, verify its token and admin status. • Long downtimes are rare; check Bots status to confirm. If the problem persists, contact support via Feedback .

## Timeouts
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_timeout.html

• Slow internet or large media can cause timeouts - retry the action. • Large imports run in the background; check progress. • If timeouts repeat, reduce file sizes or split the operation. Queued work continues once the connection is stable.

## Rate Limited
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_rate.html

• Telegram and the bot throttle very fast bursts of actions. • If you hit a rate limit, wait a few seconds and retry. • The Free plan has a monthly send cap (100 per channel) - check /stats . Premium removes the send caps entirely.

## Media Errors
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_media.html

• "File too large" - videos over up to 25MB on Free / up to 50MB on Premium. Compress or upgrade. • "Unsupported format" - use common formats (MP4, JPG, PNG, GIF, PDF). • "Media not found" - the file was removed from storage; the message becomes text-only. Re-upload the media to fix.

## Channel Errors
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_channel.html

• Bot is not an admin - add the bot as admin (Post Messages permission). • Channel not found - wrong username or link; verify @yourchannel . • Invalid format - use @username, a full invite link, or the numeric ID. • Can't connect - make sure you're the owner or an admin. Fix the cause and try connecting again.

## Forbidden
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_forbidden.html

• "Bot was kicked from the chat" - re-add the bot as admin. • "Bot can't post" - grant Post Messages permission. • "Blocked by user" - the channel owner removed the bot; re-invite it. These are Telegram permission errors - fix them in your channel settings, not in the bot.

## Payment Errors
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/error_payment.html

• "Payment failed / declined" - Telegram declined the Stars charge; check your Stars balance and try again. • "Not activated yet" - wait 2-3 min, then reopen /premium . If Stars were taken but nothing activated, contact @MaximalXP with your user ID and transaction details. Include the transaction ID when contacting support.

## No Post Sent
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/troubleshoot_nopost.html

If nothing was posted: • Confirm the bot is a channel admin with Post Messages . • Check the schedule time and timezone are correct. • Verify the sender bot is connected and online. • Look at Message List to confirm the message still exists (not deleted/expired). Use the Troubleshooting topics for permission and rate-limit fixes.

## Late Post
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/troubleshoot_late.html

If a message posts later than scheduled: • Check the channel timezone — schedule times use it. • Verify the sender bot is online and an admin. • Telegram can delay delivery under load — the bot retries. • Check the sent report for the actual posting time. Set the correct timezone to fix the issue.

## Media Fails
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/troubleshoot_media.html

If media doesn't post: • Check file size against limits (10 MB free / 100 MB Premium per item; videos up to 25MB / up to 50MB). • Make sure the file format is supported by Telegram. • Confirm the bot has permission to post media. • Corrupted uploads fail — re-upload the file. Re-schedule the message after fixing the file.

## Permission
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/troubleshoot_perm.html

Missing permissions cause most posting failures: • Make the bot an admin of the channel. • Grant Post Messages (and Delete Messages for media cleanup). • For sender bots, ensure they also have the needed rights. • If you use a private link, ensure you're the owner/admin. The bot verifies permissions automatically after you update them.

## Bot Down
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/troubleshoot_bot.html

If a sender bot stops responding: • Check that the bot is still an admin in the channel. • Reconnect the sender bot from Sender Bots . • Telegram restarts bots from time to time — wait a couple of minutes. • If messages queue up, they resume once the bot is back. If problems continue, contact support with the affected channel and bot.

Q: What do I do when a bot seems offline?
A: Reconnect the sender bot from Sender Bots and confirm it's a channel admin. Telegram restarts bots periodically — wait a few minutes before retrying.

## Scheduled Message Didn’t Post? The 6 Real Causes, In Order of Likelihood
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_post_not_sent.html

When a post misses its slot, the cause is almost always in the delivery chain — the schedule itself is the least likely suspect. Work this list top to bottom; each item fixes the majority of cases. 1. The sender bot lost its admin seat Someone cleaned up admins and removed your sender bot. Check Manage Channel → Administrators : your sender bot must be there with Post Messages . Re-add it, and the queue resumes. 2. The token was revoked or replaced A /revoke in @BotFather kills the old token everywhere instantly. If the bot shows the sender as disconnected, open Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot and paste the fresh token. 3. Permissions were narrowed Admin exists but without Post Messages — a silent killer after permission tightening. Open the admin entry and re-enable posting. 4. The channel changed identity Username changed or the channel was converted — the old link no longer resolves. Reconnect the channel; schedules are kept. 5. Telegram rate limits on bursts Telegram throttles aggressive posting bursts channel-wide. If several posts fire close together and one fails, it is usually this. Space posts by minutes, not seconds — the scheduler already does, but third-party bots added to the channel can collide with it. 6. The monthly send cap (Free) On Free, sends pause at 100 per channel per month until the 1st. The bot warns you before the cap; /stats shows the counter. Premium lifts the cap entirely. Fastest diagnosis Send /stats (status of everything) and check the sender-bot status screen. Still mysterious? /feedback with the channel and the missed time — support can see delivery attempts and will tell you exactly which step failed.

Q: Will missed posts send later automatically?
A: A post that failed delivery is marked failed, not silently retried forever. Fix the underlying cause, then delete it and schedule it again.

Q: How do I know if it was the monthly cap?
A: The bot notifies you at the cap, and /stats shows monthly usage per channel. If neither shows the cap, it was delivery-side — start the checklist from the top.

# Privacy

## Privacy
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/privacy.html

What the bot stores and why: • Telegram identifiers — your user ID and channel IDs, so the bot knows what it manages and for whom. • Content you schedule — message texts and media references, kept only to deliver your posts on time. • Settings — language, time zone, signatures, bot tokens you connect. • Operational logs — delivery results, used to fix failures and show you statistics. The bot never reads channels it is not connected to, never posts anything you did not schedule, and never shares your data with third parties. Deleting a message in the bot deletes it from storage; deleting your account deletes everything. Full details are in the website Privacy Policy.

## Your Data
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/privacy_data.html

The bot stores what's needed to run: your channels, scheduled/recurring messages, settings, and referral info. It doesn't read your other chats or messages. Media uploads are compressed and stored only for your schedules. Export or delete your data anytime - see Privacy .

## Consent
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/privacy_consent.html

By using the bot you agree to the processing of the data needed to provide the service. Accepting the Terms and Privacy Policy is required on first use. You can stop using the bot and request deletion at any time.

## Third Parties
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/privacy_thirdparty.html

We share data only where required to deliver the service: • Payment provider (Telegram Stars) for processing payments. • Telegram itself for sending your messages. No data is sold, rented, or used for advertising.

## Export Data
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/privacy_export.html

You can export a copy of your data anytime: • /export for scheduled/recurring messages. • /backup (Premium) for a full backup. This lets you take your data with you or switch services.

## Delete Account
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/privacy_delete.html

To delete your account and data, contact @MaximalXP . Deletion is permanent: messages, media, settings, and referral data are removed. Export first if you want to keep a copy.

## Token Safety
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/security_token.html

Your bot token is like a password for your sender bot. • Never share it publicly (screenshots, support chats). • If leaked, reset it in @BotFather and Replace Token in the bot. • Tokens are stored encrypted. A leaked token lets anyone post as your bot.

Q: Should I keep my bot token secret?
A: Absolutely. Never share your sender bot token or payment details in chat. Anyone with a token could post to your channels.

## Account Safety
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/security_2fa.html

• Access to the bot is tied to your Telegram account (no extra passwords). • Enable Telegram's two-step verification for extra security on your account. • Never send your bot token or payment details in plain chat to strangers. Telegram's own security settings protect your login.

Q: Do I need Telegram two-step verification?
A: Recommended. Two-step verification protects your Telegram login — and therefore your bot access and connected channels — from unauthorized use.

## Data Safety
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/security_data.html

• Your data is stored securely and used only for the service. • It's not sold or shared beyond payment processing. • Export a backup regularly ( /backup ) to keep a copy. • Request deletion anytime via @MaximalXP . See Privacy for the full policy.

Q: Where is my data stored?
A: Your data is stored by the bot and used only to run schedules. Export or backup your data anytime, and contact support for data-related requests.

## How Do I Delete My Fast Scheduler Account and All My Data?
URL: https://fastschedulebot.github.io/Fast-Schedule/help/a/qa_delete_data.html

You can leave Fast Scheduler completely — no subscriptions to cancel by email, no dark patterns, no &ldquo;are you sure&rdquo; maze. One message, and everything tied to your Telegram account is erased. How to request deletion Contact @MaximalXP in Telegram and ask to delete your account. Deletion is permanent and covers all data associated with your user ID: scheduled and recurring messages, media storage, sender-bot tokens, channel connections, settings, statistics and referral records. Export first — deletion has no undo Before deleting, create a backup with /backup (a Premium toolkit) or export individual lists, so your content plan survives the account. Once deletion runs, there is no recovery path — the data no longer exists to restore. What happens on Telegram&rsquo;s side Your sender bots keep existing in @BotFather — they are your bots, created with your account. If you want them gone too, revoke or delete them there after deletion. Revoke first if you plan to keep using them elsewhere. The bot loses admin rights relevance immediately, but you can also remove @FastSchedulerBot and your sender bot from your channels&rsquo; admin lists yourself — a good hygiene step that takes ten seconds per channel. Already-published posts stay in your channel, of course — deletion cannot rewrite history. How long data is kept normally While you are an active user, every category of data is kept only while it is useful: schedules until they are deleted or sent, bot tokens until you disconnect the bot, and account records until you delete the account. The Privacy Policy&rsquo;s retention table lists each category with its exact lifetime.

Q: Who do I contact to delete my Fast Scheduler account?
A: Message @MaximalXP on Telegram and request account deletion. The deletion is permanent and removes all data linked to your Telegram ID.

Q: Can I delete everything but keep the bot?
A: Yes — you can delete individual schedules, media and sender bots from inside the bot without deleting your account. Full deletion is only for leaving the service entirely.

Q: Should I export a backup before deleting?
A: Definitely. After deletion there is no way to restore anything, so create a backup with /backup first if there is any chance you will return.
